entries.summary: This document introduces the new Android CLI and agentic developer tools designed to streamline terminal-based workflows, AI-assisted code migrations, and automated testing. It matters because it enables modern coding agents to seamlessly inspect production crashes, render Compose previews, and manage deployments without relying solely on traditional interactive UI interfaces.

entries.title: XR is for everyone: Designing accessible spatial experiences
entries.summary: Added a new developer summit talk page documenting accessible spatial experiences in XR, providing developers with video and transcript resources to build inclusive augmented and virtual reality applications.

In this introductory guide for developers new to XR, Jazmin Cano shares the foundational accessibility principles honed at Owlchemy Labs. Engine-agnostic and universally applicable to both games and apps, this session explores how early consideration of motor, visual, auditory, and cognitive needs leads to better experiences for all users. Discover how to build an inclusive development culture, conduct meaningful testing, and design spatial interactions that remove barriers without sacrificing quality. ## Summary - Spatial interfaces risk excluding users if access needs are omitted during early design. Consider accessibility across physical and cognitive categories from the very start. - Disability affects 1.3 billion people worldwide, including roughly 20% of gamers. Designing for specific access needs often benefits a wider audience in temporary or situational contexts. - Physical accessibility features reduce body strain and accommodate limited mobility. Useful options include scalable environments (such as small human mode) and artificial snap turning. - Vision and auditory aids provide critical cues across alternate senses. Useful implementations include high-contrast object glows and directional subtitles. - Testing with diverse groups helps teams iterate effectively on spatial designs. Involve people across varied disabilities and age groups throughout development. - Developers should prototype inclusively from the beginning, test with diverse users, and make an immediate commitment to implement at least one accessible feature. ## Resources - \[XR Accessibility Project\](https://xraccessibility.github.io/) - \[GAConf\](https://www.gaconf.com/) - \[GAConf Archive\](https://www.gaconf.com/archive/) - \[Owlchemy Labs\](https://OwlchemyLabs.com) - \[Owlchemy Labs Resources and White Papers\](https://www.owlchemylabs.com/resources) ## Topics xr, entries.summary: Added documentation for the Device Manager dashboard in the Android XR Engine Hub, providing centralized tools to sideload APKs, manage XR feature permissions, execute ADB commands, filter device logs, and configure device settings.

entries.title: Capture and analyze performance traces in the Android XR Engine Hub
entries.summary: This new documentation page explains how to capture performance traces from Android XR devices using the Android XR Engine Hub and leverage Gemini for automated bottleneck analysis.

entries.title: Develop with Godot for Android XR
entries.summary: Updated the Godot Android XR documentation to expand interaction methods—such as adding mouse interaction and updating eye gaze extensions—and significantly augmented the list of supported OpenXR extensions for both the Vendors Plugin and Godot Native OpenXR to include spatial persistence, advanced foveation configurations, and new composition layers.

entries.title: Use Spatial Containers in Godot
entries.summary: Introduces guidance for using Spatial Containers in Godot for Android XR, allowing developers to render 3D OpenXR content within system-managed volumetric bounding boxes or transition to full-screen immersive mode.

entries.title: Develop with the Jetpack XR SDK
entries.summary: The Jetpack XR SDK documentation was updated to replace plain text device support labels with rich icon and link elements across all libraries (Jetpack Compose for XR, Material Design, SceneCore, ARCore, Compose Glimmer, and Projected). Additionally, the Jetpack Compose for XR section was refined to reference updated subspace component classes, and a new section was added introducing the Android XR Emulator for testing apps across headsets, wired glasses, and intelligent eyewear.

entries.title: Use a projected context to access hardware on audio glasses and display glasses
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack XR SDK documentation for accessing hardware in a projected context. The changes include improvements to audio recording code snippets with better buffer management and lifecycle handling, as well as significant expansions to camera streaming documentation. Specifically, it adds detailed guidance on dynamically querying supported resolutions and frame rates, calculating maximum frame rates using frame durations, and configuring CameraX use cases like ImageAnalysis and VideoCapture to optimize battery and thermal performance.

entries.title: Access hardware on audio glasses and display glasses
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to remove the reference to the microphone when discussing the unique hardware available on audio and display glasses, focusing instead on the camera. This minor correction ensures accuracy regarding the specific hardware features highlighted for developers building Jetpack XR SDK experiences.

entries.title: Add 3D models to your app
entries.summary: The Jetpack XR SDK documentation for adding 3D models has been updated to include key implementation details for SpatialGltfModel—such as asynchronous loading behavior, state control, and layout sizing. Note that several API reference links throughout the document were incorrectly modified to point to unrelated classes and URLs, introducing broken references that need correction.

entries.title: Access a session for creating spatialized UI and entities
entries.summary: The Jetpack XR SDK documentation for adding a session was updated to remove a caution note about activity lifecycle session invalidation and add clarification on using an optional `LifecycleOwner` parameter with the `create()` function. Additionally, minor updates were made to clarify supported contexts for Intelligent Eyewear and link to `SessionCreateResult` for session creation failures.

entries.title: Add spatial video to your app
entries.summary: Removed a caution callout regarding a known crash bug with `SurfaceEntity` and `SpatialExternalSurface` in older Jetpack XR SDK alpha versions, as the issue has been resolved in subsequent releases.

entries.title: Add a subspace to your app
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack XR SDK subspace documentation by replacing an inline list of spatial components with a reference link to spatialized components, and updated API reference links to point directly to the Subspace composable documentation.

entries.title: Bring your Android app into 3D with XR
entries.summary: The documentation updates restructure the headings for converting 2D UI components to 3D and introduce a new section on "Add spatial capabilities." These changes improve the hierarchical organization of the guide and better categorize features like spatial checks, environments, and 3D content for developers building Android XR applications.

entries.title: Enhance app experiences with perception using ARCore for Jetpack XR
entries.summary: The ARCore documentation was updated to include support for Audio & Display Glasses under applicable XR devices and clarified how sessions are created using the Jetpack XR Runtime. Additionally, new details were added regarding the `SessionCreateResult` class, session lifecycle management using an optional `LifecycleOwner`, and guidance on using projected contexts with Intelligent Eyewear. These updates help developers correctly initialize sessions and manage resources across different XR form factors.

entries.title: Work with the Geospatial API using ARCore for Jetpack XR
entries.summary: The ARCore geospatial documentation was significantly streamlined, removing detailed API setup, configuration, permissions, and code examples while updating the supported device types and providing a more concise overview of the Geospatial API and VPS capabilities.

entries.title: Anchor content at real world locations
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces Geospatial anchors for the Jetpack XR SDK, explaining how developers can place 3D content using real-world latitude, longitude, and altitude coordinates.

entries.title: Work with Geospatial poses
entries.summary: This new documentation explains how to use the Jetpack XR SDK ARCore Geospatial API to convert coordinates between device-local poses and real-world Earth-based Geospatial poses.

entries.title: Set up the Geospatial API in your app
entries.summary: This new documentation page provides a comprehensive guide on setting up and configuring the ARCore Geospatial API for Jetpack XR development. It details the necessary Google Cloud project setup, authorization methods, required permissions, session configuration modes, and how to monitor tracking states and accuracy values.

entries.title: Troubleshoot issues with the Geospatial API
entries.summary: Added a new troubleshooting guide for the ARCore Geospatial API within the Jetpack XR SDK, helping developers resolve API key authorization issues and localization quality problems.

entries.title: Get started building immersive experiences
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to include support for the `android.hardware.xr.input.face_tracking` feature flag in the app manifest. Additionally, the privacy-sensitive capabilities note was expanded to include face tracking, body tracking, scene understanding, and location, ensuring developers are properly informed about runtime permission requirements for these advanced XR features.

entries.title: Spatialized components
entries.summary: Introduces spatialized components and subspace composables in Jetpack Compose for XR, enabling developers to build adaptable spatial UI layouts that seamlessly fall back to 2D environments.

entries.title: Orbiters
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces the `Orbiter` component in the Jetpack XR SDK, explaining how developers can use it to attach contextual actions and navigation controls to spatial panels and layouts.

entries.title: SceneCore entities
entries.summary: This new documentation introduces SceneCoreEntity, a subspace composable that bridges Jetpack SceneCore and Compose for XR. It allows developers to integrate low-level SceneCore entities into Compose layouts while utilizing Compose for sizing, positioning, and modifiers.

entries.title: Spatial dialogs
entries.summary: Added new documentation for SpatialDialog in Jetpack XR SDK Compose, explaining how to implement spatialized dialogs that appear above base content with graceful 2D fallback support.

entries.title: Spatial external surfaces
entries.summary: Introduces the `SpatialExternalSurface` subspace composable for the Jetpack XR SDK, which manages Android surfaces for rendering monoscopic, stereoscopic, or DRM-protected video and image content in spatial environments.

entries.title: Spatial panels
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces the SpatialPanel composable for the Jetpack XR SDK, explaining how developers can render 2D content in a 3D space, apply subspace modifiers, and arrange multiple panels using layout components like SpatialRow and SpatialColumn.

entries.title: Arrange 3D space with subspaces
entries.summary: Introduces subspaces in the Jetpack XR SDK, explaining how to partition 3D space to build spatial layouts and add depth to apps using Jetpack Compose.

entries.title: Change how your content looks based on the display type
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces display blend modes in the Jetpack XR SDK, explaining how apps can check and adapt to different device display characteristics such as additive blending, alpha blending, and no display.

entries.title: Check device capabilities at runtime for audio glasses and display glasses
entries.summary: Added documentation and code examples for monitoring battery state changes in connected XR glasses using the Jetpack XR SDK. This addition matters because developers can now track real-time battery levels and charging states to optimize app performance, trigger power-saving modes, update UI components, and properly manage device controller lifecycles.

entries.title: Plan to support different types of audio glasses and display glasses
entries.summary: The changes in this file consist entirely of Markdown formatting updates, specifically converting relative documentation links into absolute URLs, adjusting list item markers, and removing bottom navigation blocks. Because these changes are purely formatting and structural cleanups with no technical content modifications, no developer action is required.

entries.title: Build glanceable UI with Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Introduces Jetpack Compose Glimmer, a new Compose UI toolkit tailored for building minimalist and comfortable augmented XR experiences optimized for display glasses.

entries.title: Buttons in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Introduces documentation for Button and ButtonGroup components in Jetpack Compose Glimmer, optimized for display glasses input with support for visual states, sizing variants, and focus control.

entries.title: Cards in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation introduces the `Card` and `ActionCard` components in Jetpack Compose Glimmer for XR devices, detailing their anatomy, default properties, and usage examples for building structured, interactive content containers.

entries.title: Colors in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation introduces the Jetpack Compose Glimmer color system, tailored for additive displays and real-world XR environments. It details the specialized color palette, default roles, and best practices for spatial UI design.

entries.title: Focus in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation page provides guidance on managing focus, pointer input, and navigation behavior using Jetpack Compose Glimmer for display glasses.

entries.title: Icon buttons in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Introduces documentation for the `IconButton` component in Jetpack Compose Glimmer for XR, detailing its sizing, states, defaults, and usage guidelines.

entries.title: Icons in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Added new documentation for the Jetpack Compose Glimmer Icon component, detailing proper usage for sizing, sources, tinting, and best practices on XR display glasses.

entries.title: Handle indirect pointer inputs in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Added documentation for the `onIndirectPointerGesture` modifier in the Jetpack XR SDK, enabling developers to handle high-level input events like clicks and swipes from touchpads on XR devices.

entries.title: List items in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation introduces the `ListItem` component in Jetpack Compose Glimmer, detailing how to build focus-responsive single-row elements for display glasses.

entries.title: Lists in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Introduces documentation for GlimmerLazyColumn in Jetpack Compose Glimmer, explaining how to implement performance-optimized lists tailored for touchpad navigation and focus management on XR display glasses.

entries.title: Horizontal pagers in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Introduces documentation for `GlimmerHorizontalPager`, a Jetpack Compose Glimmer component designed for horizontally scrollable layouts on display glasses with built-in snap animations, automatic page indicators, and text motion recommendations.

entries.title: Preview your Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI with composable previews
entries.summary: This new documentation explains how to use Android Studio composable previews to design and test Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI components for XR display glasses. It matters because it enables developers to quickly iterate on UI layouts and simulate additive display conditions without repeatedly deploying to a device.

entries.title: Shapes in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces the shape system in Jetpack Compose Glimmer, explaining how to use and customize small, medium, and large shapes for XR surfaces and components.

entries.title: Surfaces in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Added new documentation introducing the Jetpack Compose Glimmer `surface` component for XR development, detailing its core visual properties, interaction states, and implementation patterns for focusable and clickable elements.

entries.title: Text in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces the Text component in Jetpack Compose Glimmer for XR devices, detailing its smart color-matching capabilities, typography scaling, and usage of the Google Sans Flex variable font.

entries.title: Title chips in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces the TitleChip component for Jetpack Compose Glimmer, explaining how to use it to provide non-interactive context or labeling above components like cards and vertical lists.

entries.title: Toggle buttons in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Added documentation for the ToggleButton component in Jetpack Compose Glimmer, detailing its anatomy, size variants, state animations, and usage examples for XR display glasses.

entries.title: Vertical stacks in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: This new documentation introduces the VerticalStack component in Jetpack Compose Glimmer, detailing its 3D overlapping layout, specialized scrolling behaviors, and focus management for XR devices.

entries.title: Voice input indicator in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Added documentation for the VoiceInputIndicator Jetpack Compose Glimmer component, detailing how to capture and normalize microphone input to provide visual audio feedback in XR applications.

entries.title: What's included in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Introduces Jetpack Compose Glimmer, a UI library built on Jetpack Compose specifically tailored for building native user interfaces and experiences for AI glasses with displays.

entries.title: Create virtual devices for audio and display glasses
entries.summary: Updated the documentation for creating a phone AVD host device for glasses by specifying the exact API level (`canary-20261007`) for the API CANARY Preview, ensuring developers select the correct target version required for compatibility.

entries.title: Create virtual devices for XR headsets and XR glasses
entries.summary: Updated the Android XR Emulator system requirements note to explicitly clarify that the emulator does not support apps built with game engines like Unity, Godot, and Unreal Engine, in addition to the previously mentioned OpenXR apps. This helps developers better understand the tool's limitations before starting AVD creation.

entries.title: Run your app's augmented experiences on the emulator
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to include support for 360-degree panoramic photo environments, detailing how to use equirectangular JPG or PNG images and navigate them using the Shift key and mouse or arrow keys. Additionally, a new section was added explaining how to enable and disable the display snooze timeout using ADB commands to test power consumption and real-world battery behavior on display glasses.

entries.title: Add a subspace that follows a target
entries.summary: This new documentation explains how to use the experimental FollowTarget API in Jetpack XR SDK to create dynamic subspaces that either follow the user's head movements (like HUDs) or attach to real-world environmental anchors.

entries.title: Understand subspace modifiers
entries.summary: The subspace-modifiers documentation was updated to introduce the experimental `MovePolicy.anchor()` API, explaining how developers can allow users to snap and anchor movable elements (such as spatial panels and models) to detected real-world surfaces. The update details usage parameters like orientation and semantics, outlines necessary session configurations and permissions, and clarifies the behavior of updated move policies.

entries.title: Transition from Home Space to Full Space
entries.summary: Removed a reference to the 'Learn Android XR Fundamentals: Part 1' codelab from the transition documentation, leaving only the link to the design guidance. This streamlines the learning resources and points developers directly to foundational design principles for space transitions.

entries.title: Handle audio output for audio glasses and display glasses using Text to Speech
entries.summary: Added a promotional callout and link to the ML Kit GenAI Text-to-Speech API documentation. This matters because it informs developers building XR applications that they can optionally leverage generative AI models for more natural-sounding speech audio compared to the standard Android TTS implementation.

entries.title: Create spatial layouts
entries.summary: The Jetpack Compose for XR UI documentation has been refactored into a hub page. The detailed implementation guides, code snippets, and tutorials for spatial components like panels, orbiters, and layouts have been removed from this file and organized into separate dedicated developer guides.

entries.title: Develop with OpenXR
entries.summary: The OpenXR documentation has been updated to reflect expanded XR capabilities on Android. Key additions include new framework features like Spatial Containers, Geospatial anchors, global passthrough dimming, viewport feathering, body tracking, and image/marker tracking, alongside expanded details for existing features such as scene meshing, light estimation, and face tracking. Furthermore, new sections were added for Unreal Engine and Godot engine support, detailing how developers can build Android XR apps using these engines via OpenXR.

entries.title: Build with supported OpenXR extensions
entries.summary: Added four new Android XR OpenXR extensions (`XR_ANDROID_geospatial`, `XR_ANDROID_geospatial_anchor`, `XR_ANDROID_global_passthrough_dimming`, and `XR_ANDROID_google_cloud_auth`) targeting Spatial API version v4, introduced necessary runtime permissions for existing extensions like anchor sharing and scene meshing, and updated documentation formatting.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added new OpenXR error codes (`XR_ERROR_RUNTIME_FAILURE` to `xrDestroyGeospatialTrackerANDROID`, and both `XR_ERROR_POSE_INVALID` and `XR_ERROR_RUNTIME_FAILURE` to `xrLocateGeospatialPoseANDROID`) to improve error handling and robustness for Android Geospatial tracking.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added `XR_ERROR_POSE_INVALID` to the list of possible error returns for both `XrGeospatialTrackerANDROID` and `xrCreateSurfaceAnchorAsyncANDROID` functions. This matters because it provides developers with explicit error handling when an invalid pose is supplied during geospatial tracking or surface anchor creation.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: This new OpenXR extension introduces global passthrough dimming capabilities for optical see-through Android XR devices, allowing apps to adjust passthrough darkness while enabling the system to override dimming for safety.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added `XR_SCENE_MESH_SEMANTIC_LABEL_SET_DEFAULT2_ANDROID` to the `XrSceneMeshSemanticLabelSetANDROID` enum to support the new `XR_ANDROID_scene_meshing_semantic_label2` extension. This matters because it enables developers to utilize expanded semantic labeling capabilities for scene meshes on Android.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added the XR_SPATIAL_ANNOTATION_QUAD_ALIGNMENT_SURFACE_ANDROID enum value and its corresponding documentation to the XrSpatialAnnotationQuadAlignmentANDROID type. This addition allows developers to align spatial annotation quads coplanar with the surface of underlying objects, improving the integration of AR content with physical geometry.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: This new OpenXR extension introduces spatial bounds definitions (spheres, boxes, and frustums) that applications can use to filter and restrict the discovery of spatial entities.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Updated the OpenXR `XR_ANDROID_spatial_discovery_raycast` extension documentation to include internal anchor links for API structures, added Valid Usage Identifier (VUID) links to implicit valid usage lists, expanded the list of contributors, and removed the developer preview banner.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Introduces the XR_ANDROID_viewport_feathering OpenXR extension, which allows apps to query runtime-applied edge feathering insets on devices with small fields of view to improve visual comfort and UI layout.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Introduces spatial containers to OpenXR, allowing apps to run in 3D window-like entities so users can interact with multiple simultaneous experiences in mixed reality.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: This document introduces the `XR_EXT_spatial_container_self_rendering` OpenXR extension, which enables applications to self-render pixels for spatial containers using standard swapchains and composition layers. It defines the rendering lifecycle, state management functions, and view configuration recommendations for efficient spatial container rendering.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Updated the OpenXR spatial entity documentation to include new spatial component types (`XR_SPATIAL_COMPONENT_TYPE_GEOMETRY_POINT_ANDROID` and `XR_SPATIAL_COMPONENT_TYPE_PERSISTENCE_SCOPES_ANDROIDX1`), added corresponding error handling and configuration parameters for spatial annotation tracking, and included new context filter references for persistence structures.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added documentation for the new `XR_EXT_spatial_entity_archetypes` OpenXR extension, which introduces spatial entity archetypes to simplify querying component data by unique component combinations.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added documentation for the new XR_EXT_spatial_image_tracking OpenXR extension, which enables applications to detect and track specific planar images as spatial entities in augmented and virtual reality environments.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added documentation for the new `XR_EXT_spatial_mesh_tracking` OpenXR extension, which defines capabilities for tracking environment triangle meshes to support virtual content collision and optional watertight mesh generation.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: This new OpenXR documentation introduces the `XR_EXT_spatial_object_tracking` extension, enabling applications to track predefined physical objects and their semantic labels in a 3D space without requiring prior input datasets.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: Added support for cloud-shared spatial anchors by introducing the `XR_SPATIAL_PERSISTENCE_SCOPE_ANCHORS_FOR_CLOUD_SHARING_ANDROIDX1` scope and new context result error codes (`LOCALIZATION_FAILURE`, `MAP_FEATURE_INSUFFICIENT`, `NETWORK_FAILURE`, and `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`) under the `XR_ANDROIDX1_spatial_anchor_cloud_sharing` extension. This matters because it enables developers to handle cloud-based spatial anchor persistence and troubleshoot cloud sharing, localization, and network-related failures more effectively.

entries.title: Android XR for OpenXR
entries.summary: The changes update the OpenXR spatial plane tracking extension documentation by standardizing internal anchor links with absolute URLs, refining the list formatting for structure member descriptions and implicit valid usage, and updating the contributor list. These improvements ensure better navigation and compliance with the documentation format.

entries.title: Get started with OpenXR for Android XR
entries.summary: Updated the OpenXR get-started guide to include comprehensive instructions on configuring spatial container properties, declaring new hardware features like face tracking and precise GPS, and mapping dangerous permissions to specific OpenXR extensions to ensure proper Android XR app compliance.

entries.title: Build with Spatial Containers
entries.summary: Introduces documentation for Spatial Containers in Android XR, detailing how to use OpenXR extensions to render 3D content within bounded volumetric windows or full-screen immersive modes.

entries.title: Understand permissions for XR
entries.summary: The XR permissions documentation has been updated to include new permissions, such as `android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO`, `android.permission.BODY_TRACKING`, and `android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, along with expanded definitions for existing permissions like `EYE_TRACKING_FINE`, `SCENE_UNDERSTANDING_COARSE`, and `SCENE_UNDERSTANDING_FINE`. Additionally, numerous new OpenXR extensions and Unity features have been added across these categories to support advanced tracking, rendering, and spatial features.

entries.title: Select your development tools and technologies
entries.summary: This update cleans up document metadata by switching the source format, removing outdated Developer Preview 4 banner announcements, and fixing relative links to use absolute URLs. Additionally, terminology for glasses was slightly updated under the Jetpack XR SDK section (changing 'AI glasses' to 'audio and display glasses').

entries.title: Develop with Unity for Android XR
entries.summary: Updated the Unity XR documentation table to include new features like Bounding Box Detection, Shareable Anchors, and Spatial Container, while also expanding the description of Geospatial (VPS) capabilities to include plane tracking configuration for surface and geospatial anchors.

entries.title: Android XR Extensions for Unity
entries.summary: Added reference documentation for new Android XR Extensions for Unity, including shareable anchor management classes, spatial bounding box and spatial container features, and XR input action mapping. These additions expand the available APIs for building immersive spatial experiences and handling cross-device anchors and spatial features in Unity.

entries.title: Use Spatial Containers in Unity
entries.summary: Added documentation for Spatial Containers in Unity for Android XR, explaining how to configure managed Full Space Mode, set up project requirements, and handle runtime states and bounds.

entries.title: Develop with Unreal Engine for Android XR
entries.summary: Updated the Unreal documentation for Android XR Extensions (v1.1.0) to include support for Unreal Engine 5.6.x and 5.8.x. The update adds references to the new API reference documentation, expands the feature and OpenXR extension mapping table with links to specific C++/Blueprint classes and version numbers, introduces new capabilities such as light estimation cubemaps and viewport feathering, and provides guidance on choosing between legacy anchor persistence and the newer Spatial Entities architecture.

entries.title: Set up Direct Preview for Unreal Engine
entries.summary: Updated the supported Unreal Engine version requirement from Unreal Engine 5.6.1 or higher to specifically Unreal Engine 5.6.x or 5.8.x. This clarifies the exact engine versions compatible with direct preview for Android XR development.

entries.title: Android XR Unreal Reference
entries.summary: Expanded the Android XR Unreal Extensions API reference documentation by adding numerous new structs, classes, and Blueprint function libraries. These additions cover extended functionalities such as light estimation, anchor persistence, eye and face tracking, global dimming, passthrough mesh support, spatial raycasting, and performance metrics, providing developers with comprehensive tools for building immersive XR experiences.

entries.title: Android XR Extensions for Unreal Engine quickstart
entries.summary: Added a new 'Next steps' section to the Android XR Extensions quickstart guide for Unreal Engine. This update provides developers with direct links to the API reference, supported OpenXR extensions, and Direct Preview setup instructions to help them immediately transition from setup to building and testing their applications.

entries.title: Multitasking and multi-instance

entries.title: Migrate Health Connect from Android 13 (APK) to Android 14 (framework)

entries.title: About Credential Manager

entries.title: Android Jetpack Dev Resources - Android Developers

entries.title: Explore the Jetpack libraries by type

entries.title: Appstate Statestore

Key changes include adding support for `preferredConfig` and `maxBytesPerImage` parameters, refining the `calculateInSampleSize` logic to enforce strict per-image memory ceilings, and improving display size calculations in `getMaxWidgetMemoryAllowedSizeInBytes()` by leveraging `WindowManager` bounds on Android R and above.

This matters because it provides developers with more accurate, up-to-date visual representations of how the components appear and render within modern Android environments.

entries.title: Create an app widget with Glance
entries.summary: Added crucial developer guidance for Jetpack Glance app widgets. This includes a note emphasizing the need to explicitly call update methods after modifying state via updateAppWidgetState to ensure UI refresh, and a new section on managing widget image memory efficiently across size buckets when dealing with bitmaps and content URIs to prevent system memory limit violations.

entries.title: Handle errors with Glance
entries.summary: Added a note regarding Android 17 (API level 37) behavior changes where `AppWidgetManager.updateAppWidget` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if the serialized bitmap memory limit is exceeded. This explains how Glance catches these exceptions in `onCompositionError` and advises developers to use a lightweight, text-only `RemoteViews` fallback layout to ensure a recoverable state.

entries.title: Create a basic widget
entries.summary: Added documentation on keeping RemoteViews images within system memory limits for classic AppWidgetProvider widgets. It details best practices for avoiding memory ceiling issues on Android 17 and higher by downsampling bitmaps using WindowMetrics, using full `updateAppWidget` calls instead of partial updates for images, and using WorkManager for background processing.

entries.title: Create an advanced widget
entries.summary: Added an important warning regarding the usage of `partiallyUpdateAppWidget`. Developers are now advised to reserve this method for lightweight text or visibility updates and avoid using it for bitmap, icon, or URI image updates to prevent exceeding system bitmap memory limits due to cached memory retention.

entries.title: Buttons in Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Added documentation explaining how to customize the focus color for buttons in Jetpack Compose Glimmer. This update matters because it provides guidance on using the `focusedColor` parameter to express brand identity while maintaining optical ergonomics and readability on transparent displays.

entries.title: App Standby Buckets

entries.title: Set app memory budgets
entries.summary: Updated the app memory budgets documentation to recommend using background threads (such as `HandlerThread` for Kotlin/Java and background worker `ALooper` for NDK) when registering over-budget listeners and watchers. This prevents cache eviction and memory cleanup tasks from blocking the UI or render threads. Additionally, the guidelines now emphasize registering listeners before applying tightened memory budgets to avoid missing initial over-budget events, handling repeated callbacks by making cleanup logic idempotent, and properly managing background thread lifecycles.

entries.title: Migrate from the TensorFlow Lite Interpreter to CompiledModel
entries.summary: Updated the LiteRT migration documentation with detailed instructions for capturing golden outputs using specific ADB commands, handling tensor shapes and sizes across different element types (including uint8 exceptions), utilizing correct signature and tensor names for by-name API calls, and ensuring proper GPU accelerator logging checks during runtime verification.

entries.title: Build an Android app with the LiteRT CompiledModel API
entries.summary: Updated documentation for LiteRT 2.3.0 runtime to clarify GPU acceleration behavior and migration steps. Specifically, it details how `CompiledModel.Options(Accelerator.GPU, Accelerator.CPU)` behaves when the GPU dependency is missing (falling back to CPU silently while logging a warning) and adds guidance on running golden output capture tests using `am instrument` to prevent file deletion during test uninstalls.

entries.title: Add pointer cursors in Jetpack Compose
entries.summary: This new documentation file introduces a structured workflow for implementing custom pointer cursor behavior in Jetpack Compose applications targeting large screens and desktop environments. It matters because it provides step-by-step guidance for adding appropriate hover icons—such as grab, crosshair, resize, hand, text, and wait cursors—to enhance UI interactivity and user experience.

entries.title: Add keyboard shortcuts in Jetpack Compose

entries.title: Add tooltips in Jetpack Compose

entries.title: Animation and shared transition performance optimization
entries.summary: Clarified the mechanics of reading animated states during the Composition phase. The documentation now specifically states that reading state during composition triggers recomposition of the reading recompose scope and non-skippable children on every animation tick, rather than the entire composable tree, providing a more precise explanation of performance implications.

entries.title: Effects, lifecycle, and threading optimization
entries.summary: Updated the documentation regarding the execution order and lifecycle of Jetpack Compose effects (DisposableEffect, SideEffect, and LaunchedEffect) relative to composition changes and frame rendering. It clarifies that LaunchedEffect launches asynchronously on the composition's CoroutineContext and is not guaranteed to run after layout and draw, and cautions developers to use layout modifiers like onPlaced or onSizeChanged instead of relying on effect dispatch timing for layout bounds.

entries.title: Graphics and rendering performance optimization
entries.summary: Updated the graphics performance documentation to explicitly recommend Coil 3 (`io.coil-kt.coil3:coil-compose`) for asynchronous image loading and downsampling. This matters because specifying the modern library version helps developers avoid main-thread jank caused by synchronous bitmap decoding.

entries.title: Layouts, measurement, and coordinate performance optimization
entries.summary: The Jetpack Compose layout performance documentation was updated to provide more precise technical descriptions of how `Modifier.onGloballyPositioned` triggers performance bottlenecks during scrolling and animations. Additionally, the guidelines for local placement and bounds tracking were refined to explicitly highlight the benefits of `Modifier.onPlaced` for local coordinates and `Modifier.onLayoutRectChanged` for throttled bounds tracking using `throttleMillis` and `debounceMillis` parameters.

entries.title: Jetpack Compose performance optimization skill
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack Compose performance guidelines to clarify recomposition cost mechanics and correct technical details regarding `LaunchedEffect` execution order and coroutine dispatch behavior.

entries.title: Android intent and component security best practices
entries.summary: Updated Android intent and service security documentation to mandate more rigorous validation checks. Changes include enforcing explicit allowlists for nested intent components, clearing selector intents, clearing or rejecting URI permission grant flags, hardening `IntentSanitizer` usage with tighter constraints and robust exception handling, and requiring cross-process interfaces (such as AIDL or Messenger) for validating caller signatures in exported bound services.

entries.title: Android permission security: Audit and remediation guide
entries.summary: Updated the Android permissions security documentation to clarify correct Binder IPC context usage for `Binder.getCallingUid()`, fix local-call fallback logic in `CallerVerifier`, and explicitly warn against authenticating senders using `PendingIntent.getCreatorPackage()` or `PendingIntent.getCreatorUid()` due to spoofing risks.

entries.title: API source code for Glimmer Button component

entries.title: API source code for Glimmer projected context
entries.summary: Updated the `getProjectedDeviceId` implementation to improve virtual device selection reliability. Instead of blindly picking the first matching device name, it now filters for devices with active virtual displays (on Android 14+) and selects the most recently created device using the highest ID, preventing stale sessions from interfering with active ones.

This update informs developers about how to get their apps noticed on tablets, foldables, and other large screen devices by completing Tier 2 or Tier 1 of the adaptive app quality guidelines, and provides a link to apply for the badge.

entries.title: Widget quality
entries.summary: The widget quality guidelines documentation has been updated to clarify and expand upon several criteria across layout, content, discovery, and system coherence categories. Key updates include more precise instructions for handling widget resizability (WL-4, WL-4.1, WL-4.2), specific new sizing options for high-tier widgets (WL-2, WL-5), clearer requirements for empty and loading states (WT-1, WS-3), and refined rules for alignment and preview assets.

entries.title: Keep the screen on
entries.summary: The documentation for keeping the device screen on has been updated to remove the Java code snippet for `FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON`, leaving only the Kotlin implementation. This reflects a shift toward prioritizing Kotlin as the primary language for Android development examples.

entries.title: Testing Worker implementation
entries.summary: Removed all Java code snippets from the WorkManager testing documentation, making the guide exclusively focus on Kotlin examples.

entries.title: Schedule alarms
entries.summary: Removed all Java code snippets from the AlarmManager documentation, standardizing the guide to focus exclusively on Kotlin examples and incorporating missing immutable flags for PendingIntents.

entries.title: Common blur use cases
entries.summary: This new documentation page provides code examples and guides for implementing common UI patterns using Compose advanced blur APIs, such as progressive edge blurs, diagonal gradients, radial spotlights, and custom shader masks.

entries.title: Blurring in Compose
entries.summary: This new documentation page explains how to use Modifier.blur in Jetpack Compose to apply both uniform and advanced progressive blur effects to UI elements. It provides practical examples and API guides for controlling blur gradients, multi-stop distributions, and edge clipping.

entries.title: Simplify your WebView implementation with Jetpack Webkit
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack Webkit dependency version from 1.17.1 to 1.18.0 in the code examples. This matters because it informs developers of the latest stable library release and ensures they use up-to-date APIs.

entries.title: Beta program
entries.summary: The webview-testing documentation was updated to bump the recommended version of the `androidx.webkit:webkit` library from `1.17.1` to `1.18.0` for both Groovy and Kotlin Gradle build configurations. This ensures developers are guided to use the latest stable APIs and bug fixes available in the AndroidX Webkit library.

entries.title: Run ARCore for Jetpack XR apps on mobile devices
entries.summary: Updated the androidx.xr.arcore:arcore-play-services dependency version from 1.0.0-rc02 to 1.1.0-alpha01 in the build configuration examples. This update ensures that developers use the latest Jetpack XR SDK release candidate and alpha libraries for ARCore mobile development.

entries.title: Test your app with ARCore test rules
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack XR SDK testing dependencies (`arcore-testing` and `scenecore-testing`) from version `1.0.0-rc02` to `1.1.0-alpha01` across both Kotlin and Groovy code snippets. This ensures developers use the latest testing APIs and fixes compatible with the 1.1.0-alpha01 release cycle.

entries.title: Create your first activity for audio glasses and display glasses
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack XR runtime dependency version from 1.1.0-alpha01 to 1.1.0-alpha02 in both Groovy and Kotlin code snippets. This ensures developers use the latest APIs and bug fixes when setting up their first XR activity.

entries.title: Set up the Jetpack XR SDK
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack XR SDK dependency versions in the setup guide. This includes bumping the runtime, scenecore, compose, and arcore libraries to their latest alpha/beta releases to ensure developers use the most current APIs and bug fixes.

entries.title: Adaptive app quality guidelines
entries.summary: Added a new section promoting the Google Play Large Screen Badge. This update informs developers about how to get their apps noticed on large screen devices by completing Tier 2 and Tier 1 adaptive app quality guidelines, and provides a direct link to the application form.

entries.title: Widget quality
entries.summary: The widget quality guidelines documentation has been updated to clarify layout, sizing, and state requirements. Key changes include updated specifications for resizable widgets (WL-4, WL-4.1, WL-4.2), new expectations for handling empty and zero states (WT-1), revised minimum sizing and resizing rules (WL-2, WL-5), and enhanced guidance on system coherence such as direct error handling on the widget UI (WS-3). These updates help developers build more consistent, responsive, and accessible Android widgets.

entries.title: Game Stats
entries.summary: Added documentation detailing aggregation types (SUM, COUNT, MAX) and critical implementation requirements for Game Stats. The updates instruct developers to send per-event values rather than precomputed lifetime totals, ensuring proper integration with Google Play Games Services features.

entries.title: Play Games Sidekick
entries.summary: The Play Games Sidekick documentation was updated to revert the configuration schema for default entry point positioning. The previous attributes (`horizontal-position` and `vertical-position-percent`) were replaced back with the simpler `value` attribute supporting preset positions like `MIDDLE_LEFT` and `TOP_RIGHT`. Additionally, the feedback section at the end of the document was removed.

entries.title: Playability review process for Google Play Games on PC
entries.summary: The Google Play Games checklist documentation was updated to broaden the 'Frictionless Cloud save and restore' requirement into a more general 'Game progress sync' requirement. This change broadens the scope from specific cloud save and seamless restore implementations using PGSv2 to any cross-platform cloud sync solution.

entries.title: Googlebook
entries.summary: The Googlebook documentation was updated to include guidance on earning the Google Play Large Screen Badge. It now details the requirements for completing Tier 1 and Tier 2 adaptive app quality guidelines and provides a direct link to the badge application form.

entries.title: Get started
entries.summary: Updated the version of the lifecycleViewmodelNav3 dependency from 2.12.0-alpha04 to 2.12.0-alpha05 in the Navigation 3 get-started guide. This ensures developers use the latest pre-release version containing recent bug fixes and API improvements.

entries.title: Multiple back stacks recipe
entries.summary: Updated the multiple backstacks recipe code for Navigation 3 by replacing the custom rememberSerializable state handling with the new rememberNavKey utility. This simplifies the top-level route state management and reflects recent API updates in the Navigation 3 library.

entries.title: Device compatibility mode
entries.summary: The documentation for `OVERRIDE_EXCLUDE_CAPTION_INSETS_FROM_APP_BOUNDS` was updated to clarify its function in desktop windowing. It now details how the override prevents UI occlusion and layout misalignment by excluding caption bar insets from the app bounds and `Configuration.screenHeightDp`, and it was added to the summary table of per-app overrides while being removed from the nonfunctional list.

entries.title: A2UI Compose
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack Compose Agent-to-UI (A2UI) library documentation for the release of version 1.0.0-alpha02. This release includes dependency updates, API changes such as replacing the function list in `A2uiBasicCatalogV1` with the `A2uiBasicCatalogV1.Functions` interface to simplify customization, removing `const` from `CatalogId`, and bug fixes ensuring `A2uiProperty` list factories correctly throw exceptions for invalid `minItems` or `maxItems` values.

entries.title: A2ui
entries.summary: Updated the A2UI library documentation to reflect the release of version 1.0.0-alpha02 for both `a2ui-engine` and `a2ui-model`. This update provides developers with the latest library dependencies and release notes as of October 21, 2026.

entries.title: appfunctions
entries.summary: Android Jetpack's AppFunctions library has been updated to version 1.0.0-beta01. This release introduces several meaningful API updates—such as moving `AppFunctionName`, renaming `description` to `instructions` in metadata to align with MCP conventions, and marking resource containers as experimental—alongside crucial bug fixes for Java time deserialization, generated filename symbols on various operating systems, and URI permission handling on newer SDKs.

entries.title: Camera Feature Combination Query
entries.summary: The Camera Feature Combination Query library has been updated to version 1.7.0-rc01, transitioning the 1.7.0 release from alpha to a release candidate stage. This update includes dependency updates for both the base library and the play services query provider, signaling increased stability ahead of a stable release.

entries.title: camera viewfinder
entries.summary: The Camera Viewfinder library has been updated to version 1.7.0-rc01 across all artifacts (viewfinder-compose, viewfinder-core, and viewfinder-view). This release candidate bumps the `compileSdk` for Compose libraries to 37.1, which requires updating the `compileSdk` for dependent apps and libraries.

entries.title: CameraX
entries.summary: AndroidX CameraX 1.7.0-rc01 has been released, promoting CameraX from alpha to release candidate status. This update introduces important API changes by converting several Camera2 interoperability interfaces into abstract classes, improves Low Light Boost behavior with a 'last setting wins' policy alongside flash support, and fixes critical OpenGL thread crashes, memory/surface leaks, and JDK compatibility issues.

entries.title: Compose Animation
entries.summary: Updated the Compose Animation library documentation to include the release of version 1.13.0-beta02. This update increments the latest beta release version and updates the latest update date to October 21, 2026, allowing developers to track and adopt the newest bug fixes and improvements.

entries.title: Compose Foundation
entries.summary: Jetpack Compose Foundation version 1.13.0-beta02 has been released. This update introduces a more performant implementation for `Modifier.border` that supports generic and polygon shapes via runtime shaders (with fallback flags available), includes rendering fixes for rounded rectangle outlines, and resolves a prefetching bug in the cache window.

entries.title: Compose Material
entries.summary: The Compose Material documentation was updated to release Version 1.13.0-beta02, advancing the latest update date to October 21, 2026, and including the corresponding release notes and commit logs.

entries.title: Compose Material 3
entries.summary: This update bumps the Compose Material3 adaptive navigation suite and overall library dependencies to version 1.5.0-beta02. It also introduces version 1.0.0-alpha02 of the `material3-a2ui` artifact, adding an animated shimmer effect for loading states and refactoring `A2uiBasicCatalogV1` to use an `A2uiBasicCatalogV1.Functions` interface for better customization.

entries.title: Compose Remote Foundation
entries.summary: Updated the Compose Remote Foundation library to version 1.0.0-alpha05, bumping dependencies and adding release notes for this version.

entries.title: remote compose
entries.summary: Released version 1.0.0-alpha22 of the Jetpack Compose Remote libraries, introducing the new `remote-creation-expression` library, adding support for environment and time variables via `RemoteTimeVariables` and `RemoteConfiguration`, and providing several API improvements and bug fixes regarding animations, text styling, and touch handling in the player.

entries.title: Compose Runtime
entries.summary: Added release notes for Jetpack Compose Runtime version 1.13.0-beta02, highlighting a critical bug fix for a memory leak in `ComputedState` and an invalidation issue related to `Snapshot.withoutReadObservation`. This update also updates the latest stable release date and beta version references in the release table.

entries.title: Compose UI
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to reflect the release of Jetpack Compose UI version 1.13.0-beta02, including its release date and corresponding commit range. This update matters for developers tracking the latest beta progression of Compose UI to test new fixes and features before the stable release.

entries.title: Compose
entries.summary: Updated Jetpack Compose library versions to their latest beta releases (beta02) across animation, foundation, material, material3, runtime, and ui groups, along with the corresponding latest update dates of October 21, 2026. This allows developers to test the newest pre-release bug fixes and improvements.

entries.title: DataStore
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack DataStore documentation to reflect the stable release of version 1.3.0. This release introduces major new features including KMP web storage support (`sessionStorage`, `localStorage`, and OPFS), native encryption via `datastore-tink`, Android tracing integration, the new `DataStore.Builder` API using structured concurrency, and baseline profiles for startup performance. It also details key API promotions, bug fixes like improved `CorruptionException` messages, and dependency updates across all DataStore artifacts.

entries.title: Exifinterface
entries.summary: Added release notes for androidx.exifinterface:1.5.0-alpha01, which bumps the default minSdk from API 21 to API 23, removes obsolete @RequiresApi(21) annotations, and fixes isSupportedMimeType parsing support for HEIC and AVIF.

entries.title: Glance Wear
entries.summary: Glance Wear has been updated to version 1.0.0-alpha21. This release introduces the new `GlanceWearProfiles.wearWidgets` RemoteCompose profile for Glance Wear widgets and updates the library dependencies.

entries.title: ink
entries.summary: Updated Jetpack Ink libraries to version 1.1.0-alpha10, which introduces bug fixes such as adding anti-aliasing to the cut edges of strokes edited using the partial stroke eraser.

entries.title: Lifecycle
entries.summary: Android Jetpack Lifecycle libraries have been updated to version 2.12.0-alpha05. This release introduces new SavedStateContainer integration APIs in SavedStateHandle—including asContainer(), getOrCreateContainer(), and getOrCreateSavedStateHandle()—while adding a breaking change where combining getStateFlow and getLiveData on a SavedStateHandle will now throw an IllegalArgumentException.

entries.title: Media3
entries.summary: This release introduces Android Media3 version 1.12.0-alpha01, adding support for Display P3 color space, a centralized experimental feature flags registry, subtitle time offsets, and new media metadata properties. It also brings numerous improvements and bug fixes across ExoPlayer, Extractors, Audio, Video, Muxers, CompositionPlayer, Transformer, and Session modules.

entries.title: Mediarouter
entries.summary: Released version 1.9.0-rc01 of the androidx.mediarouter library, advancing the release candidate stage and updating the latest release table accordingly.

entries.title: navigation3
entries.summary: Navigation 3 has been updated to version 1.3.0-alpha03, updating the latest release date to October 21, 2026, and bumping the runtime and UI library dependencies accordingly. This release contains no functional changes from version 1.3.0-alpha02.

entries.title: Palette
entries.summary: The stable release of AndroidX Palette version 1.1.0 has been published, highlighting the adoption of JSpecify nullability annotations since version 1.0.0. This update provides improved null-safety guarantees for Kotlin and Java interoperability.

entries.title: photopicker
entries.summary: Released version 1.0.0-alpha03 of the Photopicker library, introducing major API changes, artifact renaming (such as renaming `androidx.photopicker:photopicker` to `androidx.photopicker:photopicker-embedded`), lower minSdk support down to API 23, and updates to Compose compileSdk and dependency requirements.

entries.title: Room 3.0
entries.summary: Room version 3.1.0-alpha03 has been released, introducing key API additions such as `setPreparedStatementCacheSize` for configuring prepared statement caches and `allowDataLossOnRecovery` for handling database corruption. This update also bumps the Kotlin target requirement to version 2.2 and includes bug fixes for KSP type alias resolution and DAO queries with non-deterministic relations.

entries.title: Savedstate
entries.summary: Androidx SavedState version 1.6.0-alpha05 has been released. This update introduces the new `SavedStateContainer` API as a common implementation base for `SaveableStateRegistry`, `SavedStateHandle`, and `SavedStateRegistry`, alongside new `asContainer()` and `getOrCreateContainer()` methods on `SavedStateRegistry` for managing child containers.

entries.title: Sqlite
entries.summary: AndroidX SQLite has been updated to version 2.8.0-alpha03, which introduces updates requiring the libraries to target and be compiled with Kotlin 2.2.

entries.title: Test Backup
entries.summary: Updated the documentation for the Automated Backup Restore Test framework to release version 1.0.0-alpha03. This release introduces new features like simplified test setup, @Nested class configuration inheritance, direct controller injection, and device serial pinning, alongside numerous bug fixes addressing test stability, timeouts, database and SharedPreferences helpers, and dependency cleanup.

entries.title: text-vertical
entries.summary: AndroidX text-vertical libraries have been updated to version 1.0.0-beta03, marking the intended final beta release. This version introduces a new 'Subtitle Cue' sample tab to demonstrate various rendering and span capabilities, fixes multiple layout and background bugs related to RubySpan and EmphasisSpan, updates Compose dependencies, and improves AnnotatedString handling.

entries.title: Tracing
entries.summary: AndroidX Tracing version 2.0.5 has been released. This update includes a critical bug fix for a race condition in pool management that could cause deadlocks when the same thread concurrently flushed and released packets, particularly while using an EmptyCoroutineContext.

entries.title: Wear Remote Compose Material 3
entries.summary: Wear Compose Remote Material3 has been updated to version 1.0.0-alpha14. This release introduces new components like RemoteSegmentedCircularProgressIndicator, RemoteTextToggleButton, and RemoteIconToggleButton, alongside dynamic color support via dynamicRemoteColorScheme. It also adds RemoteMotionScheme, replaces RemoteCurvedProgressIndicator with RemoteIntroOutroCurvedProgressIndicator for timers and goals, and includes various bug fixes and typography updates.

entries.title: Wear Compose
entries.summary: Released Wear Compose version 1.8.0-alpha02, introducing several API updates and bug fixes. Key highlights include renaming pull-to-refresh indicator classes, adding a delay customization parameter to one-handed gestures, introducing a content lambda overload for status bar suppression, removing experimental feature flags for warped curved text and swipe-to-reveal dual fling thresholds, and resolving visual glitches and scroll offset issues in components like TimeText, TransformingLazyColumn, and PullToRefreshBox.

entries.title: Wear
entries.summary: AndroidX Wear release notes updated to include the release of `androidx.wear:wear-core:1.2.0-beta01` on October 21, 2026. This beta release progresses the wear-core library toward a stable 1.2 release, allowing developers to test new pre-release APIs and fixes.

entries.title: Webkit
entries.summary: AndroidX Webkit version 1.18.0 has been released as stable, bringing important new features and API updates. Key additions include profile-level APIs for managing Cross-Origin Isolation (allowing SharedArrayBuffer usage for trusted origins on an allowlist), a new prefetch queue draining control constant (`WEBVIEW_NAVIGATE_DRAIN_PREFETCH`), and several API modernizations such as renaming `PrefetchParameters#isJavaScriptEnabled` to `includeClientHints` and `Profile#addQuicHints` to `preferQuicFor`.

entries.title: ARCore for Jetpack XR
entries.summary: Jetpack XR ARCore has been updated to release version 1.0.0 and version 1.1.0-alpha01. Version 1.0.0 marks the library's stabilization, bringing core augmented reality capabilities such as motion tracking, persistent anchors, hit testing, and geospatial poses. Version 1.1.0-alpha01 introduces new spatial tracking and annotation APIs (`SpatialAnnotation`, `SpatialAnnotationTrackingOptions`, `TestSpatialAnnotation`), enhanced geospatial accuracy metrics, critical bug fixes for memory leaks and concurrency in `AugmentedImageRenderer`, and lifecycle dependency updates.

entries.title: Jetpack Compose for XR
entries.summary: AndroidX XR Compose has been updated to version 1.0.0-beta02. This release introduces several API changes including Kotlin 2.2 targeting, updates to `FollowMode.soft()`, optimizations for `PitchLimits` via `@JvmInline`, removal of deprecated items like `SpatialActivityPanel` overloads and `DragPolicy`, and the deprecation of stateless sliders. Additionally, it brings important bug fixes such as resolving a constraints crash with Orbiters, optimizing `SubspaceLayoutNode` allocations, updating lifecycle dependencies, and highlighting a known memory leak issue related to the SceneCore dependency.

entries.title: Jetpack Compose Glimmer
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack XR Glimmer library to version 1.0.0-alpha22, introducing several API updates and bug fixes. Key changes include making the AlertDialog text parameter optional and reordering it, renaming container-specific AlertDialog styling parameters for clarity, adding focused background color properties to ToggleButton and IconToggleButton, and improving Modifier.border to support generic polygon shapes via runtime shaders along with fixes for rounded rectangle rendering.

entries.title: XR Projected
entries.summary: AndroidX XR Projected libraries have been updated to version 1.0.0-alpha14. This release introduces new APIs like ProjectedActivityCompat methods for managing input focus on displayless devices, enables battery state testing in ProjectedTestRule, updates the lifecycle-runtime dependency to version 2.10.0 for AGP compatibility, and fixes host device context issues in isProjectedDeviceConnected alongside dependency updates to alpha14 across all projected artifacts.

entries.title: XR Runtime
entries.summary: Jetpack XR Runtime version 1.0.0 has been promoted to stable, and version 1.1.0-alpha02 has been released. The 1.1.0-alpha02 update introduces dynamic mesh update APIs, renames several Quad creation methods, updates Kotlin targeting to 2.2, adds SPATIAL_API_V4, and includes critical bug fixes addressing context leaks, lifecycle scope issues in XrDevice, and session management behavior.

entries.title: Jetpack SceneCore
entries.summary: Jetpack XR SceneCore has officially reached stable status with the release of version 1.0.0, introducing core capabilities for placing 3D content, spatial audio, and environments. Additionally, version 1.1.0-alpha01 has been released, bringing new dynamic mesh update APIs, runtime bounding box modifications, stable glTF animation APIs, and dependency updates.

entries.title: AndroidX releases
entries.summary: Updated AndroidX library versions for the October 21, 2026 release cycle. Key updates include promoting App Functions (`appfunctions`) to 1.0.0-beta01, advancing Camera (`camera`, `camera.featurecombinationquery`, `camera.viewfinder`) to 1.7.0-rc01, advancing various Jetpack Compose libraries to beta02 and alpha05 releases, and updating A2UI protocol components to 1.0.0-alpha02.

entries.title: Recent Release Notes
entries.summary: Android Jetpack documentation has been updated with a new release entry for October 21, 2026. This update includes version bumps and new stable, beta, and alpha releases across various libraries, notably Compose (v1.13.0-beta02), Camera (v1.7.0-rc01), Datastore (v1.3.0), and multiple XR-related libraries (arcore, runtime, scenecore), helping developers track the latest stable and experimental features.

entries.title: Alpha Releases
entries.summary: Added a new release entry for October 21, 2026, detailing alpha updates across various Jetpack libraries including Compose, Lifecycle, Media3, Navigation3, Room3, and XR-related components. This update tracks the latest early-access pre-release versions for developers testing upcoming Android features.

entries.title: Beta Releases
entries.summary: Added release entries for October 21, 2026, introducing beta updates for various Jetpack libraries including Appfunctions 1.0.0-beta01, multiple Compose components (version 1.13.0-beta02 and Material 3 1.5.0-beta02), and XR Compose 1.0.0-beta02. This matters because it tracks the latest pre-release milestones leading up to stable versions for these core Android and Jetpack libraries.

entries.title: RC Releases
entries.summary: Added release candidate entries for October 21, 2026, including updates for Camera (version 1.7.0-rc01), Camera Featurecombinationquery (version 1.7.0-rc01), Camera Viewfinder (version 1.7.0-rc01), and Mediarouter (version 1.9.0-rc01). This matters for developers tracking the latest stable precursors for Jetpack libraries.

entries.title: Stable Releases
entries.summary: Added a new release entry for October 21, 2026, documenting stable updates for various AndroidX libraries including Datastore 1.3.0, Webkit 1.18.0, and the initial 1.0.0 releases for new XR libraries (xr-arcore, xr-runtime, and xr-scenecore). This matters for developers tracking the latest stable Jetpack APIs and adopting Android XR development tools.

entries.title: Android KTX
entries.summary: Updated the dependency version for `androidx.palette:palette-ktx` from `1.0.0` to `1.1.0` in the documentation. This update ensures developers use the latest stable release containing recent bug fixes, performance improvements, and potential new APIs.

entries.title: List of KTX extensions
entries.summary: Updated the dependency version for `androidx.palette:palette-ktx` from `1.0.0` to `1.1.0` in the KTX extensions documentation. This update ensures that developers copy and paste the latest stable release for their Android projects.

entries.title: Kotlin Multiplatform
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) readiness table with the latest library versions and release dates as of October 2026. This includes version bumps for Compose Runtime, DataStore, Lifecycle, ViewModel, Navigation3, Paging, SavedState, and SQLite, reflecting ongoing progress in bringing core Android libraries to multiplatform environments.

entries.title: Set up DataStore for KMP
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack DataStore dependencies (`datastore-core` and `datastore-preferences-core`) from version 1.2.1 to 1.3.0 in the multiplatform documentation. This update ensures developers use the latest stable APIs and bug fixes provided in the 1.3.0 release.

entries.title: Set up Room database for KMP
entries.summary: Updated the Room version from '3.1.0-alpha01' to '3.1.0-alpha03' in the KMP setup documentation. This ensures developers use the latest pre-release version with bug fixes and improvements when configuring Room in their multiplatform projects.

entries.title: Android latest updates
entries.summary: This update highlights the latest Android development tool and library releases. Android Studio advances to Rabbit 2 RC 1, Jetpack Compose libraries step up to beta02 releases (1.13.0-beta02 and 1.5.0-beta02), and core CameraX artifacts graduate from alpha to the 1.7.0-rc01 release candidate stage.

entries.title: CameraX architecture
entries.summary: Updated the recommended CameraX library version in the architecture documentation from version 1.7.0-alpha03 to the release candidate version 1.7.0-rc01 for both Groovy and Kotlin Gradle dependency snippets. This ensures developers are directed to use the latest stable release candidate for building camera-enabled features.

entries.title: CameraX video capturing architecture
entries.summary: The CameraX video-capture documentation has been updated to include instructions and code examples for several advanced features: QHD video resolution support, 10-bit HDR dynamic range configuration, video stabilization, real-time audio amplitude monitoring via AudioStats, and high-speed or slow-motion video recording using HighSpeedVideoSessionConfig.

entries.title: Media3 ExoPlayer
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to improve readability, fix a broken migration guide link, and format the introductory tip using standard Markdown callout syntax.

entries.title: Core Compose
entries.summary: The Compose customization documentation for Media3 UI was updated to remove obsolete `visible` and `AnimatedVisibility` parameters from control slot examples, reflecting recent API simplifications in the Compose player controls.

entries.title: Android Studio Preview
entries.summary: Updated the Android Studio download links and version references across the documentation from Rabbit 1 (2026.2.1 RC 2) to Rabbit 2 (2026.2.2 RC 1) for Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms.

entries.title: Release notes for Android Studio preview
entries.summary: The Android Studio preview features documentation was updated to change the release channel for Android Studio Rabbit 2 from Canary to RC (Release Candidate). Additionally, several major feature sections were removed from the document, including Compose Preview Screenshot Testing, Model Assignment for AI tasks, cross-platform app migration tooling for iOS, Flutter, and React Native, and direct publishing to Google Play for testing.

entries.title: Android Studio Rabbit 2 Closed Issues
entries.summary: Added release notes for Android Studio Rabbit 2 | 2026.2.2 RC 1, including its companion Android Gradle Plugin 9.5.0-rc01 release and minor bug fixes. This update tracks the latest stabilization progress leading up to the final release.

entries.title: DataStore
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack DataStore library dependencies across all artifacts (Preferences, Proto, Core, and RxJava support modules) from version 1.2.1 to version 1.3.0. This ensures that developers copying the setup code will use the latest stable release containing recent bug fixes and performance improvements.

entries.title: Set app memory budgets
entries.summary: The app memory budgets documentation was updated to reflect changes in the manifest syntax, removing the requirement to explicitly declare a default `<process />` entry and clarifying how to apply budgets only to specific subprocesses. Additionally, a new note was added specifying that per-process memory budgets require Android Gradle Plugin 9.5.0 (or 9.6.0-alpha01) or higher.

entries.title: App-driven profiling
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack Tracing library dependency version from 2.0.4 to 2.0.5 in both Kotlin DSL and Groovy build configuration snippets. This ensures developers use the latest stable version with bug fixes and improvements when implementing profiling and tracing.

entries.title: Migrate from Material 2.5 to Material 3 in Compose for Wear OS
entries.summary: The Wear Compose migration guide has been updated to reference version 1.8.0-alpha02 across the Material3, Foundation, and Navigation libraries. This matters for developers as it ensures they use the correct synchronized dependency versions and API references for the latest pre-release features and updates.

entries.title: Navigation 3
entries.summary: Updated the core Navigation 3 dependencies (`navigation3-runtime` and `navigation3-ui`) from version `1.3.0-alpha02` to `1.3.0-alpha03` in both Groovy and Kotlin Gradle snippets. This ensures developers use the latest library version with recent bug fixes and API improvements.

entries.title: Preview your UI in Compose for Wear OS
entries.summary: Updated the `androidx.wear.compose:compose-ui-tooling` dependency version from `1.8.0-alpha01` to `1.8.0-alpha02` in the Wear OS Compose previews documentation. This ensures developers use the latest alpha release containing fixes and updates for Wear OS UI tooling and multipreview annotations.

entries.title: Get started with widgets
entries.summary: Updated the dependency versions for Wearables widgets and Remote Compose libraries in both Groovy and Kotlin build configuration snippets. This ensures developers use the latest alpha releases (such as bumping Remote Compose to alpha22 and Glance Wear to alpha21) to access recent bug fixes and API updates.

entries.title: Android 17 QPR 2 GSI binaries and release notes
entries.summary: Updated the Android 17 QPR2 Generic System Image (GSI) release documentation to point to a different build version (reverting/updating from beta7.1/CP41.260831.019 to beta6.1/CP41.260831.007.A3). This includes changing all flash tool links, download buttons, SHA-256 checksums, and filenames across ARM64 and x86_64 architectures with and without GMS to ensure developers download the correct and current build.

entries.title: OTA images for Google Pixel
entries.summary: Updated the Android 17 QPR3 device OTA images documentation with new build numbers (DP11.261002.005), a later release date of October 20, 2026, a refreshed security patch level of 2026-10-05, updated Google Play services versions, and new download links and SHA-256 checksums for all supported Pixel devices.

entries.title: Factory images for Google Pixel
entries.summary: Updated the Android 17 QPR3 Beta download documentation to point to Beta 2 (cinnamonbun-qpr3-beta2), featuring new build IDs (DP11.261002.005), updated factory image URLs and SHA-256 checksums for supported Pixel devices, an updated release date of October 20, 2026, and a newer security patch level and Google Play services version.

entries.title: Get Android 17 QPR 3

entries.title: Jetpack Compose Performance
