Additionally, the guide was refined to provide more accurate details on stability concepts, suggest adding `contentType` parameters alongside keys in lazy layouts, and mention `computedStateOf` as an alternative to `derivedStateOf` starting in Compose 1.13.

entries.title: Backwards Write
entries.summary: The Jetpack Compose backwards-write documentation has been updated to add an explanatory note clarifying the exact definition of a backwards write (`Read -> Write` order requirement) and addressing the overhead of immediate state overwrites. Additionally, rule 1 was expanded to include `onPlaced` and `onLayoutRectChanged` as layout modifiers that should not write to state read in composition, and minor typos were corrected.

entries.title: Follow best practices
entries.summary: This update expands Jetpack Compose performance best practices with crucial guidance on `remember`, lazy layouts, and state derivation. It adds warnings about expensive `equals()` keys in `remember`, outlines comprehensive performance guidelines for lazy lists (including bundle-saveable keys, content types, and avoiding `indexOf`), introduces `computedStateOf` as a lighter alternative to `derivedStateOf` in Compose Runtime 1.13+, and provides clear criteria for choosing the right state derivation approach.

entries.title: Modifier breakdown by phase
entries.summary: Updated the Compose modifier phases documentation to discourage the use of `Modifier.composed` in favor of `Modifier.Node`, clarify placement and layout observation callbacks (such as `onSizeChanged`, `onPlaced`, and `onGloballyPositioned`), and add recommendations for handling global coordinates efficiently via `requireLayoutCoordinates()`.

entries.title: Stability in Compose
entries.summary: Updated the documentation regarding Jetpack Compose stability and collections to advise caution when replacing standard collections with immutable collections or stability annotations. The change clarifies that structural equality checks (`.equals()`) on every recomposition can be more costly than recomposition itself, removing the specific O(1) and O(N) complexity references while maintaining the core recommendation.

entries.title: Diagnose stability issues
entries.summary: Updated the Compose stability documentation to emphasize the behavior and performance implications of Strong skipping mode. New notes and explanations clarify that relying solely on recomposition counts can be misleading, and that leaving collection-holding models unstable under strong skipping mode can improve performance by avoiding expensive structural `.equals()` checks in favor of instance equality (`===`).

entries.title: Fix stability issues
entries.summary: Updated Jetpack Compose stability fixing guide to reflect modern Compose behavior (where strong skipping mode is the default in Kotlin 2.0.20+). The documentation now advises caution when using immutable collections and stability annotations (`@Immutable`, `@Stable`) with standard collection types, highlighting performance pitfalls like redundant structural `.equals()` comparisons in lazy layouts.

entries.title: Strong skipping mode
entries.summary: The strong skipping documentation was updated to modernize callout formatting and expand the guidance on annotating classes as stable. Specifically, it clarifies the use of `@Stable` and `@Immutable` with object equality, and adds important trade-off considerations regarding automatic stability inference in Compose modules, performance impacts of cheap `.equals()` checks, and potential performance pitfalls when annotating models containing collections.

entries.title: Tooling
entries.summary: The Compose performance tooling documentation has been updated to clarify that recomposition counts should not be used as a substitute for actual benchmarks. It adds important context explaining that skipping a composable still carries overhead (slot table and parameter comparison), and that skipping intermediate composables saves less time than deferring rapidly changing state reads to the Layout or Draw phases. Developers are advised to always verify performance improvements using composition tracing and Macrobenchmark.

entries.title: Google Play Billing Library release notes
entries.summary: Google Play Billing Library has been updated to improve error categorization for external payment flow drop-offs. Specifically, when a user abandons an external payment flow (such as an e-wallet) without returning to the app, the response code is now correctly reported as `BillingResponseCode.USER_CANCELED` with a `BILLING_ACTIVITY_PAUSED` debug message instead of defaulting to a generic `BillingResponseCode.ERROR`. This matters for developers as it provides more accurate analytics and cancellation tracking for alternative billing methods.

entries.title: Integrity verdicts
entries.summary: Documented a new licensing requirement for Play Integrity verdicts on Android 13 and higher. Specifically, optional device labels like `MEETS_BASIC_INTEGRITY` and `MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY` are now omitted if the requesting app is not licensed by Google Play, and the `UNEVALUATED` status has been updated to reflect this unlicensing condition. This matters for developers as sideloaded apps or apps not distributed via Google Play may see missing or unevaluated integrity signals on newer Android versions.

entries.title: Bitmaps and memory
entries.summary: Added a new 'Common bitmap memory pitfalls' section to the documentation, detailing three major anti-patterns that lead to severe memory spikes: decoding overscaled bitmaps instead of downsampling, high concurrent retention caused by parallel decoding tasks, and leaving transient bitmaps unrecycled in high-frequency frame-processing loops. This update helps developers identify and prevent out-of-memory issues and `lmkd` kills by providing best practices, code examples, and guidance on leveraging `ImageDecoder`, limited coroutine dispatchers, and explicit recycling.

entries.title: Analyzing Java memory
entries.summary: Added a new guide section in java-memory.md on hunting duplicate strings and hydration bloat using AHAT, along with remediation strategies like bounded LRU caches instead of indiscriminate String.intern() usage. It also updated the Perfetto tracing configuration example to increase buffer size, add process stats and ftrace data sources, configure heapprofd for native and ART heaps, and extend the trace duration.

entries.title: Memory locality and performance
entries.summary: Added a new section on pointer chasing in Java and Kotlin data structures to the memory locality documentation. This addition explains how managed language reference graphs and boxed primitives cause cache misses, details how to diagnose these performance bottlenecks using `simpleperf` counters, and provides actionable recommendations for improving memory locality in managed Android code.

entries.title: Service bindings and process states
entries.summary: Added a new section detailing common service binding anti-patterns—such as forgotten unbind calls, co-locating bound services with memory-intensive UIs, and omitting priority-waiving flags—alongside actionable remedies to help developers prevent memory leaks and unnecessary process elevation.

Additionally, the guide expands on request authentication, detailing a multi-layered verification strategy that involves validating the `credId` session nonce, verifying the calling package via `getCallingPackage()`, and inspecting `request.callingAppInfo`.

entries.title: Annotation

entries.title: appfunctions
entries.summary: The Jetpack AppFunctions library has been updated to version 1.0.0-alpha12. This release includes several API changes such as requiring metadata for `AppFunctionData#serialize`, adding reified helpers and new request properties like `activityId`, introducing experimental registration APIs, and removing `AppFunctionContext` and `AppFunctionConfiguration`.

entries.title: Collection

The latest 1.5.0 alpha brings source-breaking changes to `Slider` and `RangeSlider` APIs, internal migrations to `TextFieldState` for date and time components, and performance optimizations for `DatePicker`.

entries.title: Compose Remote Foundation

This release introduces new conversion APIs, adding `ImageVector.toRemoteImageVector()` and `RemoteImageVector.vectorResource(@DrawableRes id: Int)` to allow converting Compose UI ImageVectors and drawable vector resources into RemoteImageVectors.

entries.title: remote compose

This release introduces new public APIs for animations and shared elements (`animateRemoteFloatAsState`, `RemoteModifier.sharedElement`, etc.), expands `RemotePathScope` capabilities with path shape helpers and curve overloads, adds support for Animated Vector Drawables (AVD), incorporates custom event handler operations, and includes various bug fixes and performance improvements.

These version bumps ensure developers are informed of the newest stable and alpha/rc iterations available for cross-platform development.

entries.summary: The DataStore dependency configuration was updated to use the multiplatform-compatible core artifacts (`datastore-core` and `datastore-preferences-core`) instead of the standard Android artifacts. This change matters because it enables correct resolution and usage of Jetpack DataStore within Kotlin Multiplatform common source sets.

entries.title: Set up Room database for KMP
entries.summary: Updated the Room and SQLite dependency versions in the Kotlin Multiplatform documentation (`room3` updated to `3.1.0-alpha01` and `sqlite` to `2.7.1`). This matters for developers following the guide as it ensures they use the latest alpha release containing recent fixes and improvements.

entries.title: Create a basic video editing app using Media3 Transformer
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack Media3 library dependencies (transformer, effect, and common) from version 1.11.0 to 1.11.1 in both Kotlin and Groovy code snippets. This ensures the documentation reflects the latest stable patch release.

entries.title: Create a basic media player app using Media3 ExoPlayer
entries.summary: Updated the Jetpack Media3 library dependencies from version 1.11.0 to 1.11.1 across Kotlin and Groovy code snippets. This ensures developers copy the latest stable patch version when setting up ExoPlayer, UI, common, and session modules.

entries.title: Getting started with CastPlayer
entries.summary: Updated the Media3 dependency versions from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1 across both Kotlin and Groovy code snippets in the CastPlayer creation guide. This ensures developers reference the latest stable release containing bug fixes and improvements.

entries.title: Common Media Client Data (CMCD)
entries.summary: Fixed syntax and typographical errors in the CMCD documentation code snippets for both Kotlin and Java. This ensures that the code examples for configuring custom Common Media Client Data (CMCD) properties and setting up the DefaultMediaSourceFactory are syntactically correct and can be successfully copied and used by developers.

entries.title: DASH
entries.summary: Updated the ExoPlayer DASH dependency version from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1 in the documentation snippets. This ensures developers reference the latest stable release containing bug fixes and improvements.

entries.title: Getting started

entries.title: HLS

entries.title: AndroidX Media3 migration guide
entries.summary: Updated the ExoPlayer migration guide documentation to reference AndroidX Media3 version 1.11.1 across code snippets and GitHub permalinks, ensuring developers use the latest stable release and accurate reference links.

entries.title: Getting started
entries.summary: Updated the Media3 dependency versions in the getting started guide from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1 for Kotlin and Groovy snippets. This ensures developers reference the latest patch release when integrating the transformer, effect, and common modules.

entries.title: Getting started with Compose-based UI
entries.summary: Updated the Media3 UI Compose dependency versions from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1 for both Kotlin and Groovy snippets. This ensures developers use the latest stable release containing bug fixes and improvements.

entries.title: Getting started with Views-based UI
entries.summary: Updated the `androidx.media3:media3-ui` dependency version from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1 in the installation instructions. This ensures developers use the latest patch release containing bug fixes and improvements.

entries.title: Understand device security state
entries.summary: This new documentation introduces the AndroidX Security State Jetpack library, explaining how apps can assess real-time device security posture, granular component patch levels, and update availability to gate high-risk operations.

entries.title: Release notes for Android Studio preview
entries.summary: Android Studio now includes automated migration tooling in the New Project Wizard to convert existing iOS, Flutter, and React Native projects into native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose-based Android apps. This feature matters because it streamlines cross-platform transitions with an integrated progress UI that handles task planning, code transformation, and compilation checks.

entries.title: Baseline Profiles overview
entries.summary: Updated the recommended Macrobenchmark library dependency version from `1.4.1` to `1.5.0` in the Baseline Profiles overview documentation. This change ensures developers adopt the latest stable features, performance improvements, and bug fixes provided by the newer library version.

entries.title: Set app memory budgets
entries.summary: This new documentation explains how apps can declare static or dynamic memory budgets to help the system optimize RAM usage through page eviction, compression, and swap.

entries.title: Inspect rendering speed
entries.summary: The GPU rendering inspection documentation has been updated to modernize Jetpack Compose-specific descriptions for rendering stages (such as Draw, Measure/Layout, and Input Handling & Animation) and to remove outdated information regarding legacy Android versions (4.0 to 5.0) and the GPU overdraw visualization section.

entries.title: App-driven profiling
entries.summary: Updated the androidx.tracing library dependency versions from 2.0.1 to 2.0.2 in the build configuration examples. This ensures developers use the latest stable release containing bug fixes and performance improvements when setting up the Profiling Manager.

entries.title: Build a templated media app
entries.summary: The documentation for building media apps for Android Auto was updated to correct a missing feature name in the manifest configuration instructions. It now explicitly specifies `android.software.car.templates_host.media` as the required feature to set to `android:required="false"` when distributing a single APK, which prevents installation issues on incompatible devices.

entries.title: Build your content hierarchy
entries.summary: Updated reference links throughout the content hierarchy documentation, shifting several API references from the `androidx.media` package to the `android.support.v4.media` package and updating MediaConstants links to point directly to the GitHub repository. This matters as it ensures developers are directed to the correct, currently utilized reference implementations and source code paths for media browser services.

entries.title: Apply content styles
entries.summary: Updated reference links across the documentation to point directly to the androidx/media GitHub repository source code instead of the Android developer reference pages, ensuring developers target the correct Media3 legacy session constant definitions.

entries.title: Implement custom browse actions
entries.summary: Updated API references and reference links in the custom browse actions documentation. This includes updating `MediaBrowserServiceCompat` references to use `android.support.v4.media` and replacing several AndroidX MediaConstants reference links with direct links to the androidx/media GitHub repository.

entries.title: Implement distraction safeguards
entries.summary: Updated the reference link for `METADATA_KEY_IS_ADVERTISEMENT` from the official Android developer documentation to the corresponding source file in the AndroidX Media GitHub repository. entries.title: Build video apps for Android Automotive OS
entries.summary: Updated the documentation for parked video apps in cars to reference the newer Media3 `MediaStyleNotificationHelper.MediaStyle` class instead of the legacy `androidx.media` version. entries.title: Google Play on Android Automotive OS

entries.title: Save data in a local database using Room

entries.title: Android TV overview

entries.title: Accessibility best practices for Android TV

entries.title: Build TV playback apps

entries.title: Behavior changes: all apps
entries.summary: Android 18 restricts implicit URI grants. Previously, the system automatically granted read and write URI permissions for `ACTION_SEND`, `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE`, and `ACTION_IMAGE_CAPTURE` intents. Now, apps must explicitly grant these permissions using the appropriate flags (e.g., `FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION`). The document also provides Kotlin and Java code examples and guidance on how to detect and address this change using `StrictMode` and logcat filtering. This change enhances security by requiring apps to explicitly manage URI permissions.

entries.title: Webkit
entries.summary: This update introduces version 1.17.0-alpha01 of the AndroidX Webkit library. The release includes a new method, `WebViewCompat#navigate`, offering enhanced navigation control, deprecates `SpeculativeLoadingParameters` in favor of more specific alternatives, adds methods to `Profile` for managing prerendering, and removes experimental APIs superseded by stable ones. These changes provide developers with improved tools for web view management and optimization.

entries.title: ARCore for Jetpack XR
entries.summary: This document details the changes in the xr-arcore library, specifically highlighting the release of version 1.0.0-alpha14. Key changes include API modifications like deprecating `GeospatialMode.VPS_AND_GPS` in favor of `GeospatialMode.SPATIAL` and introducing `GeospatialMode.INERTIAL`, custom anchor exception classes, and an `ArCoreTestRule` API. It also addresses known issues with geospatial tracking and includes an external contribution adding an `AugmentedImage` API.

entries.title: Material Design for XR
entries.summary: This document details the changes in the xr-compose-material3 library, specifically updates to alpha releases. Key changes include API modifications to the Orbiter composable and the addition of movable modifiers for SpatialPanels and SpatialExternalSurface, enhancing XR UI development. These changes allow for more flexible and streamlined spatial UI creation.

entries.title: Jetpack Compose for XR
entries.summary: This document details the release of androidx.xr.compose library version 1.0.0-alpha14. Key changes include the introduction of `transformingMovable`, removal of `SpatialGltfModel.fromData()`, updates to modifier nodes and interaction policies, and an upgrade to Compose `compileSdk` to API 37, which necessitates a minimum AGP version of 9.2.0. These changes provide new functionalities for 3D movement and layout and enhance the compatibility and stability of the xr-compose library.  It also contains a list of API changes for developers to be aware of.

entries.title: Jetpack Compose Glimmer

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 17 or higher

This change aims to prevent OTP hijacking by temporarily withholding the SMS_RECEIVED_ACTION broadcast and filtering SMS provider database queries. Apps relying on SMS OTPs should migrate to SMS Retriever or SMS User Consent APIs to maintain functionality.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 17 or higher
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces OTP (One-Time Password) protection for standard SMS messages. To mitigate OTP hijacking, apps targeting API level 37 or higher will experience a three-hour delay before standard SMS messages containing an OTP become available. This change impacts apps that extract OTPs from SMS messages, and developers should migrate to SMS Retriever or SMS User Consent APIs to maintain functionality. Exceptions exist for certain system apps. Additional protections for WebOTP and SMS Retriever formats remain unaffected.

entries.title: Behavior changes: all apps
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces enhancements to protect user privacy, specifically regarding SMS messages containing one-time passwords (OTPs). The update extends the existing SMS Retriever protection to WebOTP format messages, delaying access to these messages for apps not associated with the message's domain. This change aims to enhance security by ensuring only legitimate apps can access verification codes and impacts all apps regardless of their target API level. Apps should transition to SMS Retriever or SMS User Consent APIs.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 17 or higher
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) to enhance user privacy by encrypting the Server Name Indication (SNI) in TLS handshakes. This prevents network observers from easily identifying the domains an app connects to. The changes involve modifying how ECH is enabled and how developers can configure it through Network Security Configuration files. Specifically, ECH is now consistently used, not just opportunistically, and developers can configure it using "enabled" or "disabled" modes instead of "opportunistic". ECH GREASE is also introduced. This change enhances user privacy and provides developers with greater control over network security.

entries.title: Behavior changes: all apps
entries.summary: Android 17 blocks cross-profile loopback traffic by default.  This change affects all apps on Android 17 or higher, preventing loopback communication between different profiles, while loopback traffic within the same profile remains unaffected.

entries.title: Release notes
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces a new restriction by blocking cross-profile loopback traffic by default. entries.title: Content resolvers
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to enhance clarity and provide more robust guidance on mitigating vulnerabilities associated with the ContentResolver. The changes include improvements in the formatting, specifically utilizing callout boxes to highlight important notes. Additionally, the document now emphasizes the importance of validating URIs, offering multiple code examples, and provides clear instructions on how to handle different scenarios, such as when dealing with non-exported or permission-protected content providers. The document also suggests best practices for permission handling and emphasizes the risks associated with maintaining denylists, advocating for a more robust approach using package prefixes.

entries.title: Custom Permissions
entries.summary: This document discusses the risks associated with custom permissions in Android, including typos, orphaned permissions, and misuse of the `android:protectionLevel` attribute. It explains how these issues can lead to security vulnerabilities and provides mitigation strategies such as using lint checks and employing signature permissions.

entries.title: Dynamic Code Loading
entries.summary: This document on dynamic code loading has been updated to improve readability and clarity. Changes include formatting adjustments, such as line breaks and spacing, and wording improvements to better explain the risks associated with dynamically loading code in Android applications and the recommended mitigations.

entries.title: Improperly Exposed Directories to FileProvider
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to clarify and emphasize the importance of secure `FileProvider` configurations. It stresses the risks of exposing sensitive data through misconfiguration, particularly focusing on the dangers of using `<root-path>` and sharing broad path ranges. It also includes recommendations for URI validation, permission management, and the avoidance of `<external-path>` for sensitive data.

entries.title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Secrets
entries.summary: The documentation for hardcoded cryptographic secrets was updated. The changes include reformatting the 'Note' section using a different markdown syntax. The documentation provides information about the risks associated with hardcoding cryptographic secrets, such as keys, and how attackers could retrieve them. It then suggests using KeyChain or Android Keystore APIs for secure key storage to mitigate these risks.

entries.title: Implicit intent hijacking
entries.summary: The documentation provides an overview of implicit intent hijacking, a security vulnerability where malicious apps can intercept intents. It describes the potential impact, such as data exfiltration or arbitrary action execution, and provides mitigation strategies like using explicit intents and avoiding sensitive data in implicit intents.

entries.title: Insecure broadcast receivers
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to improve readability and clarify specific points. Changes include improved formatting, clearer descriptions of the vulnerability and its implications, and more precise explanations of mitigation strategies. These revisions aim to enhance understanding and guide developers toward more secure broadcast receiver implementations.

entries.title: Insecure machine-to-machine communication setup
entries.summary: This document provides guidance on securing machine-to-machine communication in Android applications. The changes include improved formatting, clearer explanations of risks, and more detailed mitigation strategies for various communication channels like Bluetooth, BLE, NFC, Wifi P2P, and USB. The updated content emphasizes the importance of data validation and application-level security measures to prevent attacks such as eavesdropping, malicious data injection, and device impersonation.

entries.title: WebView – Native bridges
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to improve clarity and formatting. Changes include minor wording adjustments, improved code examples, and enhanced descriptions of the risks associated with insecure WebView native bridges, specifically those related to addJavascriptInterface, postWebMessage and postMessage methods. There are also updated mitigation strategies.

entries.title: Intent redirection
entries.summary: The documentation for Intent Redirection has been updated to provide a more detailed explanation of the risks associated with this vulnerability. The update also clarifies mitigation strategies, including the use of IntentSanitizer and PendingIntent, and provides more comprehensive guidance on debugging and security hardening solutions introduced in Android 16.

entries.title: Log Info Disclosure
entries.summary: The documentation for log info disclosure has been updated to improve readability and formatting. Specifically, the document clarifies the risks of logging sensitive data to logcat, reiterates the importance of sanitizing logs in production, and provides examples of how to do so, including tokenization, data masking, redaction, and filtering.

entries.title: Path traversal

entries.title: Pending intents

entries.title: Sticky Broadcasts

The changes primarily involve minor formatting adjustments, updates to links, and improved clarity in explaining the security vulnerabilities of sticky broadcasts, specifically regarding the limitations of package name filtering and the potential for attackers to modify or access sensitive data. These updates clarify the security concerns and best practices for developers.

entries.title: Unsafe Deserialization
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to improve readability and clarity.  The primary changes involve reformatting of text, improved descriptions, and updated links to reflect the current best practices for avoiding unsafe deserialization vulnerabilities.

entries.summary: This document describes the security risks associated with using the Android DownloadManager, highlighting vulnerabilities such as permission bypass, SQL injection, and information disclosure through request headers. It explains how these weaknesses can be exploited and recommends using alternative methods like Cronet for secure downloads.

entries.title: Webviews – Unsafe URI Loading
entries.summary: The documentation for unsafe URI loading was updated with improved clarity and formatting. The changes clarify the risks associated with improper URI validation when loading content into a WebView. It emphasizes the importance of validating both the scheme and host, and provides guidance on how to properly validate hostnames in Kotlin. The document now also has improved formatting and wording.

entries.title: Improperly trusting ContentProvider-provided filename
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to clarify the risks associated with trusting filenames provided by a `FileProvider` from another application, especially regarding potential file overwriting. The changes include improvements in text formatting, rewording for clarity, and minor edits to code examples.

entries.title: Use of native code

entries.title: Weak PRNG

entries.title: WebViews – Unsafe File Inclusion
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to remove the title 'WebViews – Unsafe File Inclusion' and updated links. The primary change recommends using `WebViewAssetLoader` instead of older methods for accessing local file system assets, addressing a vulnerability related to the `file://` scheme.

entries.title: Zip Path Traversal
entries.summary: The documentation updates include minor edits to the description of the Zip Path Traversal vulnerability, emphasizing the importance of validating ZIP-extracting code and ensuring the destination directory is safe before extraction. These changes clarify potential security risks associated with handling compressed archives and provide more explicit guidance on mitigation strategies to prevent file overwrites and potential application compromise.

Specifically, the default mode for ECH has been changed from "opportunistic" to "enabled" in Android 17 (API level 37). Additionally, the documentation now clarifies the default behavior and available modes for domain encryption, including an explanation of how the `mode` attribute affects ECH behavior and GREASE use, and how it defaults based on target SDK version.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 17 or higher
entries.summary: This document introduces several behavior changes in Android 17. These include stricter background audio restrictions for apps targeting API level 37, impacting how background audio playback and focus requests are handled, requiring foreground services with specific capabilities. It also describes a change to Bluetooth RFCOMM socket behavior, where `read()` now returns `-1` when the socket is closed, aligning with standard Java `InputStream` behavior and potentially affecting apps that rely on `IOException` for connection termination.

entries.title: Behavior changes: all apps
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces app memory limits based on device RAM, aiming for a more stable environment. It also discusses leak detection, integration with Android Studio's LeakCanary, and provides details on how to identify if your app is affected via ApplicationExitInfo and trigger-based profiling.

entries.title: Background audio hardening
entries.summary: This document describes changes to background audio restrictions in Android 17. The update clarifies the requirements for background audio playback, audio focus requests, and volume changes, emphasizing the need for a visible activity or a foreground service that is not a SHORT_SERVICE. It also introduces more specific requirements for apps targeting API level 37 and highlights the conditions under which the WIU requirement is waived for apps using the exact alarm permission. The document explains why these changes were introduced and how to test for compliance.

entries.title: Features and APIs
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces a new anomaly detection service integrated with ProfilingManager. This allows developers to receive profiling artifacts triggered by system-detected performance anomalies, such as excessive binder calls and memory usage. The new `TRIGGER_TYPE_ANOMALY` trigger provides developers with heap dumps for memory issues and stack sampling profiles for binder transactions, enabling proactive debugging before system-imposed enforcements like app termination.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes
entries.summary: Android 7.0 improves battery life and reduces RAM usage through enhancements to Doze mode and background optimizations.  Doze extends its power-saving features even when the device is not stationary. Furthermore, the system restricts implicit broadcasts like `CONNECTIVITY_ACTION`, `ACTION_NEW_PICTURE`, and `ACTION_NEW_VIDEO` to reduce unnecessary app wake-ups. This is important because it changes how apps receive and respond to network connectivity and media events, which could impact background processing and user experience.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes
entries.summary: Android 7.0 introduces stricter file permission restrictions to enhance security. Apps targeting Android 7.0 or higher have restricted access to their private directory, and attempts to use `MODE_WORLD_READABLE` or `MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE` will trigger a `SecurityException`. Sharing files via `file://` URIs is prohibited, and the `FileProvider` class is the recommended way to share files between apps.  This is important because it changes how apps handle file access and sharing, requiring developers to adopt more secure practices.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes
entries.summary: To share files between applications, you must send a `content://` URI and grant temporary access permissions.  The `FileProvider` class is the recommended approach. This is important because it changes the way apps share files, requiring a shift to using content URIs and temporary permissions for security.

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.1.3 (March 2015)

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.3.1 (August 2015)

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.0.0 (April 2016)

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.1.0 (April 2016)

These changes provide developers with faster builds and the ability to utilize newer Java features.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.2.0 (September 2016)
entries.summary: This release of the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) includes improvements to Gradle, native code integration with CMake and ndk-build, auto-downloading of SDK components, an experimental build cache, enhanced APK signing, and improvements to the Jack compiler. entries.title: Android Gradle plugin 9.0.1 (January 2026)

Users need to update their projects to be compatible with built-in Kotlin, switch KMP projects to the Android Gradle Library Plugin for KMP, update build files, and update custom build logic to reference the new DSL and API. Compatibility with AGP 9.0 also requires updating third-party plugins and addresses several deprecated APIs.  A notable change is the removal of the option to opt-out of the new DSL in AGP 10.0.

entries.title: NDK Revision History
entries.summary: NDK r23 removed GNU binutils (excluding GAS), deprecated GDB, and announced the end of support for non-Neon devices and Jelly Bean in the upcoming release.  These changes require developers to migrate away from deprecated tools and features.

entries.title: NDK Revision History

entries.title: NDK Revision History

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.0.1 (January 2015)
entries.summary: This release of the Android plugin for Gradle (AGP) fixes several issues. It addresses a Gradle build failure related to `extractReleaseAnnotations`, a problem with the `--no-optimize` setting in dex bytecode generation, manifest merger problems with libraries targeting older SDK versions, and a density ordering issue when using JDK 8 in Android Studio. These fixes improve build stability and compatibility.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This release of the Android plugin for Gradle (AGP) version 1.1.1 includes several bug fixes and enhancements. It modifies build variants to optimize Wear app builds, shifts dependency-related failures to build time for easier debugging, and fixes the `android.getBootClasspath()` method. Additionally, it provides links to relevant Android developer resources.

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.1.3 (March 2015)
entries.summary: This release fixes a ProGuard failure caused by duplicated dependencies in test apps and resolves a JDK 7 error related to a non-compliant Comparator implementation.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.3.0 (July 2015)
entries.summary: This release of the Android Gradle plugin (1.3.0) introduces several enhancements. Key changes include the ability to control the task thread pool size, exclusion of LICENSE files by default, improved unit test support for multi-flavor and build variant source folders, support for instrumentation test-runner arguments from the command line, and the ability to specify additional AAPT parameters. These changes provide developers with more flexibility in configuring their builds, improved testing capabilities, and better control over the build process.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This update to the Android Gradle plugin, revision 1.3.1, addresses several bug fixes. These include fixes for ZipAlign, Renderscript packaging with NDK, support for the createDebugCoverageReport task, handling of the archiveBaseName property, and a lint warning. These fixes improve the build process and ensure correct application packaging.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This release of the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) version 2.1.0 introduces several improvements. Key changes include support for the N Developer Preview, JDK 8, and Java 8 language features using the Jack toolchain. It also adds default support for incremental Java compilation and dexing-in-process to improve build speeds. These changes enhance development workflows and support the latest Android features.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document details the release notes for Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 3.0.0, highlighting performance improvements, new features, and changes in the plugin. Key improvements include faster build times through optimizations like better parallelism, per-class dexing, and the use of AAPT2. New features include variant-aware dependency management, support for Android Instant Apps, built-in Java 8 support (with Jack deprecation), and enhanced testing capabilities with Android Test Orchestrator.  It also includes updates to Gradle and SDK build tools versions.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 3.2.0 (September 2018)
entries.summary: This document describes the release notes for Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 3.2.0. The changes include support for Android App Bundles, improved incremental build speeds with annotation processors, a migration tool for AndroidX, and a new code shrinker (R8). It also details behavior changes and bug fixes related to desugaring, AAPT2, native multidex, and other plugin improvements.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 3.4.0 (April 2019)
entries.summary: This release introduces new lint check dependency configurations for better control over lint checks in Android libraries. It also enables R8 by default for improved build performance and deprecates `ndkCompile`, encouraging the use of CMake or ndk-build. Furthermore, there is a deprecation warning for the Android Instant Apps Feature plugin and an opt-in setting for enforcing unique package names.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers

The changes include updates to Gradle and SDK Build Tools requirements, support for package visibility in Android 11, improvements to the Build Analyzer, Java 8 library desugaring in D8 and R8, and the introduction of the buildFeatures block to enable or disable build features.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 4.1.0 (August 2020)
entries.summary: This document details the changes in Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 4.1.0, including new features like exporting native libraries from external builds in AARs using Prefab, improved R8 support for Kotlin metadata, and behavior changes such as the removal of the Android Gradle plugin build cache and renaming of some properties.  It also deprecates the io.fabric Gradle plugin.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 7.0.0 (July 2021)

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 7.3.0 (Sep 2022)  |  Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This release introduces several changes, including support for custom C/C++ build systems via Ninja, a minimum Kotlin plugin version requirement (1.5.20), the enabling of archived APK generation by default, and a deprecation warning for the `package` attribute in the manifest file.  These changes enhance build flexibility, enforce dependency compatibility, and improve the build process.

entries.title: Content providers can help an application manage access to data stored by itself or stored by other apps and provide a way to share data with other apps. They encapsulate the data and provide mechanisms for defining data security. Content providers are the standard interface that connects data in one process with code running in another process.
entries.summary: This document provides an introduction to Content Providers, explaining their purpose in managing data access, sharing data between applications, and providing a standard interface for data interaction. The document highlights the advantages of using content providers, such as secure data access and the ability to modify data storage implementations without affecting other applications. It also lists the classes that rely on the ContentProvider class and scenarios where you need to implement your own Content Provider.

entries.summary: This document, which provides guidance on selecting appropriate identifiers for Android apps, has been updated. entries.title: Android Jetpack Dev Resources - Android Developers
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to include direct links to Jetpack documentation and resources, updated descriptions for Jetpack libraries, and improved formatting for better readability.

entries.title: AndroidX overview

entries.summary: This document lists class mappings from the old support library packages to the new `androidx` packages. The changes include updating the URL in the title, updating links, and minor formatting changes.

The primary change is the deprecation of the `androidx.ads` library, recommending migration to the Advertising ID API available in Google Play Services.  Additionally, there are minor updates to links and formatting to match the new documentation standards.

entries.title: Annotation
entries.summary: The documentation for androidx.annotation has been updated. The changes include dropping support for x86 based Mac and iOS KMP targets, adding the RequiresFlag annotation, adding ANNOTATION_TYPE target to RequiresApi and RequiresExtension, requiring KGP 2.0.0 or newer for projects released with Kotlin 2.0, and updating the @Discouraged retention policy. There are also updates to the table of contents and various links.

entries.title: Appcompat  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes changes in the Appcompat library. The updates include fixes for compatibility issues with ComposeView within AppCompatDialog and performance improvements for SupportMenuInflater. Also, new features are added such as support for getting per-app locales in non-Activity contexts with new APIs and `setLineHeight` for TextView compat classes.

entries.title: appfunctions  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes the changes made to the appfunctions library in the AndroidX Jetpack.  The changes include new features, API changes, and bug fixes across multiple releases, including support for Parcelables, APIs for platform request/response conversion, and improvements to error handling and metadata generation.

entries.title: AppSearch  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document introduces updates for AppSearch library, including version 1.2.0-alpha01, released on March 25, 2026. This version includes API changes such as disabling and hiding delete propagation API, new built-in types, and added functionalities like Action Accumulator API and  `AppSearchResult#RESULT_UNAVAILABLE` result error code, along with bug fixes.

entries.title: Architecture Components Release Notes Archive  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document archives the release notes for Architecture Components. It covers WorkManager, Navigation, and Paging library updates, including bug fixes, new features, and breaking changes. Each section details the changes in specific releases, providing insights into the evolution of these components.

entries.title: Architecture Components Release Notes Archive  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Architecture Components Release Notes Archive  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This release fixes an issue where previously-cancelled children of successfully completed parent work would still run and properly initializes logging classes.

entries.title: Architecture Components Release Notes Archive  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This release introduces new features like the handling of secondary menu items and AppBarConfiguration enhancements. It also includes breaking changes to argument parsing from deep links and methods used within the NavigationUI methods. The release also deprecates the android.arch.navigation:navigation-testing artifact.

entries.summary: The release includes a breaking API change where androidx.work.Result has been moved to be an inner class of ListenableWorker.

entries.summary: This release has no changes from 2.1.0-beta01.

entries.summary: This document archives release notes for the Test components that shipped in the support library. entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: Android 7.0 enhances Doze mode to further improve battery life by applying restrictions even when the device is in motion. Apps targeting Android 7.0 must adapt to these changes by using alternatives like JobScheduler to handle network operations and connectivity changes.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: To improve the security of private files, Android 7.0 restricts access to the private directory of apps. Apps targeting Android 7.0 or higher will receive a `SecurityException` if they try to use `MODE_WORLD_READABLE` or `MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE`. Additionally, the sharing of file:// URIs is prohibited, and the recommended method to share files is using `FileProvider`.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: Android 7.0 enforces the `StrictMode` API policy by prohibiting the exposure of `file://` URIs outside your app. Apps must use `content://` URIs and grant temporary access permissions, preferably through `FileProvider`, to share files with other applications.

entries.title: Verifying app behavior on the Android runtime (ART)  |  App quality  |  Android Developers
entries.summary:
The document has been updated to reflect the following changes:

*   **JNI:**  More rigorous JNI checks, proper exception handling (e.g., `NoSuchMethodError`, `NoSuchFieldError`) in functions like `RegisterNatives`, `GetFieldID`, `GetStaticFieldID`, `GetMethodID`, and `GetStaticMethodID`. Added guidance on the correct usage of `Get...ArrayElements()` and `Release...ArrayElements()` with concurrent copying garbage collection.
*   **Garbage Collection:** Emphasizes the use of the concurrent copying (CC) collector and the importance of avoiding techniques incompatible with compacting GC.
*   **Stack Size Issues:** Highlights that explicit stack size settings need review because ART has a unified stack, unlike Dalvik.
*   **Object Model:** Addresses issues where Dalvik allowed overriding package-private methods, which ART now warns against.

entries.title: Verifying app behavior on the Android runtime (ART)  |  App quality  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: These changes are important because they directly impact app stability and performance on ART. The stricter JNI checks and proper exception handling prevent unexpected crashes and memory corruption. Correctly handling garbage collection and stack sizes ensures optimal resource management. Adhering to the object model changes ensures code behaves as intended. Following the guidance in this document helps developers create more robust and ART-compatible applications, thereby improving the user experience on modern Android devices.

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.0.1 (January 2015)
entries.summary: This release of the Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.0.1, addresses several issues. It fixes a Gradle build failure related to the `extractReleaseAnnotations` module, resolves a problem with the `--no-optimize` setting for dex bytecode, corrects manifest merger issues with libraries targeting older SDK versions, and resolves a density ordering issue when using Android Studio with JDK 8. These fixes improve build stability and compatibility.

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.1.0 (February 2015)
entries.summary: This release of the Android plugin for Gradle (AGP) version 1.1.0 introduces several improvements, including enhanced unit test support with new tasks, source folders, and dependency configurations.  It also modifies test task names, ProGuard configuration, and dependency management. Finally, it adds support for the `anyDpi` resource qualifier and improves project evaluation and IDE sync speeds for projects with multiple modules. These changes improve testing capabilities and build performance.

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.1.2 (February 2015)
entries.summary: This release of the Android plugin for Gradle (AGP) version 1.1.2 includes bug fixes. Key changes include normalizing paths for mockable JAR creation, resolving the `archivesBaseName` setting issue in `build.gradle`, and correcting the unresolved placeholder failure in the manifest merger when building a library test application. These fixes improve the build process and ensure more reliable application builds.

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.3.1 (August 2015)
entries.summary: This release fixes several issues. Notably, it addresses a problem with the ZipAlign task when using custom filenames, resolves issues with Renderscript and NDK packaging, and fixes a lint warning that occurred outside of Android Studio. These changes improve build stability and provide a more robust development environment.

entries.title: Android plugin for Gradle, revision 1.5.0 (November 2015)
entries.summary: This release of the Android plugin for Gradle (1.5.0) introduces several enhancements, including the integration of the Data Binding plugin, a new Transform API for manipulating compiled class files, improved MultiDex support, and support for vector drawables. These changes aim to improve build performance, provide more flexibility for developers, and enhance compatibility with different Android versions.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.0.0 (April 2016)
entries.summary: This release of the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) version 2.0.0 introduces Instant Run, incremental build support, and dex process control for faster builds. It also includes an experimental code shrinker for debug builds and enhancements to resource shrinking, along with changes to APK signing and fixes for dependency issues.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.2.0 (September 2016)
entries.summary: This release of the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) version 2.2.0 introduces several enhancements, including Gradle 2.14.1 for performance improvements and security fixes, the ability to link native sources with CMake or ndk-build, auto-download of missing SDK components, an experimental build cache feature, improved APK signing with v2 signature scheme, and support for the android:extractNativeLibs flag.  It also includes improvements to the Jack compiler and annotation processing.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.3.0 (February 2017)
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in the Android Gradle Plugin 2.3.0. Key improvements include the use of Gradle 3.3 for performance enhancements, a build cache feature to speed up clean builds, and support for changes in Instant Run.  Additionally, there are improvements in configuration times for large projects and fixes for constraint layout library issues. The plugin also updates to ProGuard version 5.3.2 and includes bug fixes.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 3.0.0 (October 2017)
entries.summary: This document details the release notes for the Android Gradle Plugin 3.0.0, highlighting performance improvements, new features, and breaking changes. Key improvements include faster build times through better parallelism, dependency management, and incremental build processes. New features encompass variant-aware dependency management, support for Android Instant Apps, built-in Java 8 support (with Jack deprecation), enhanced testing capabilities, and more.  The document also details the minimum and default versions of Gradle and SDK Build Tools required and provides guidance on the effort needed to migrate projects.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in Android Gradle Plugin 3.1.0. Key changes include the introduction of the new D8 dex compiler, behavior changes regarding ABI splits and resource configuration, and fixes for dependency recognition and project sync errors.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers

Several behavior changes and bug fixes are also documented.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes the release notes for Android Gradle Plugin 3.3.0. Additionally, there are behavior changes related to lazy task configuration, R8 usage, faster R class generation, and single-variant project sync. Finally, there are bug fixes for RenderScript and other issues.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 3.4.0 (April 2019)

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 15 or higher
entries.summary: This document outlines behavior changes in Android 15, focusing on foreground service (FGS) behavior. Key changes include time limits for `dataSync` and `mediaProcessing` FGS types, a new `mediaProcessing` FGS type, and restrictions on launching FGS from `BOOT_COMPLETED` receivers and when holding the `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` permission. These changes aim to improve system resource management and user experience.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 15 or higher
entries.summary: Android 15 introduces a 6-hour time limit within a 24-hour period for `dataSync` foreground services.  After this limit, the system calls `Service.onTimeout()`. Apps must call `stopSelf()` within a few seconds, or an exception occurs. This change prevents excessive background service usage. Developers should implement `onTimeout()`, monitor service duration, and consider alternative APIs or user interaction to reset the timer.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 15 or higher
entries.summary: Android 15 introduces a `mediaProcessing` foreground service type, also subject to the 6-hour time limit. Developers need to manage service lifecycles and consider alternatives like WorkManager to avoid exceptions. The introduction of this new type reflects the importance of managing media-related background tasks efficiently.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 15 or higher
entries.summary: Android 15 restricts `BOOT_COMPLETED` broadcast receivers from launching certain foreground service types, including `dataSync`, `mediaProcessing`, and others. This change aims to improve system startup performance and resource usage by limiting the actions that can be initiated during device boot.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 15 or higher
entries.summary: Apps holding the `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` permission are now restricted from starting foreground services.  This change enhances user privacy and security by limiting the ability of apps with broad system-level permissions to run unrestricted background services.

These changes are important for developers to ensure their apps behave correctly on Android 15 and adhere to the updated system limitations.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 17 or higher  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) to enhance user privacy by encrypting the Server Name Indication (SNI) in TLS handshakes. This prevents network observers from easily identifying the domain an app is connecting to. ECH is opportunistically used for TLS connections if the app's networking library and the server support it. Developers can customize this behavior using the `<domainEncryption>` element in the Network Security Configuration file.

entries.title: DragAndDrop

entries.title: Drawerlayout  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in the DrawerLayout library. Key changes include integration with Android 13's OnBackPressedInvoked APIs for handling the back button when the drawer is open, and ensuring open() and close() methods work correctly even when the drawer is locked.

entries.title: Dynamicanimation  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document details the changes in the Dynamicanimation documentation. Key updates include API reference and link updates, dependency declaration instructions, and version release notes for the `androidx.dynamicanimation` and `androidx.dynamicanimation-ktx` libraries, including bug fixes, and API changes such as hiding the AnimationHandler class visibility and using JSpecify nullness annotations.

entries.title: Emoji2
entries.summary: This document describes the changes to the Emoji2 library. The key updates include support for Emoji 15.1, bidirectional emoji selector UI, and multi-skintone emoji selection, along with other bug fixes and API enhancements. These changes improve the user experience and provide more up-to-date emoji support.

entries.title: Enterprise  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document contains updates to the Enterprise Feedback documentation, including changes to dependency declarations, feedback mechanisms, and version release notes.  It also includes updated links and formatting for improved readability and clarity.

entries.title: Exifinterface
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in the Exifinterface library. The changes include bug fixes, API changes, and new features, such as support for reading and writing XMP data from HEIF and AVIF images. Several bug fixes address issues with parsing and saving image files, including WebP and JPEG formats, and the handling of XMP data.

entries.title: Glance Wear  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in the Glance Wear library. The primary updates include the release of version 1.0.0-alpha06, which introduces features like defining operations for Wear Widgets profiles and API changes such as renaming CONTAINER_TYPE_FULLSCREEN to CONTAINER_TYPE_TILE_COMPAT.

entries.title: graphics
entries.summary: This document describes the changes made to the graphics library in the AndroidX Jetpack. The updates include new features such as shape editor, SVG path import, and improvements to the feature mapping algorithm for shape morphing. It also incorporates bug fixes and API changes related to bounds calculation and polygon features.

entries.title: Health Connect  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in the Health Connect library. Key updates include the introduction of new fields to ExerciseSessionRecord and ExerciseSegment, additions to support activity intensity, a new function for HealthConnectClient to set a soft limit for the number of change logs returned, and bug fixes.

entries.title: Heifwriter
entries.summary: This document describes the changes made to the Heifwriter library. The primary change in version 1.2.0-alpha01 is the introduction of the `EncoderPreference` class. This class allows developers to specify preferences for encoder selection, such as hardware or software encoding, and the enforcement of Constant Quantization (CQ).

entries.title: Hilt
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in the Hilt documentation, including updates to links, version information, and API changes. Notable changes include the relocation of `hiltViewModel()` APIs for Compose to a new artifact and package, as well as the addition of assisted injection support and KSP support.

entries.title: ink  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document describes the changes to the AndroidX Ink library. It includes updates to dependencies, bug fixes, and new features like an emoji highlighter and Compose interoperability modules. Significant API changes were also made, including changes to angle units, shear/skew naming, and the removal of certain methods.

entries.title: Input  |  Jetpack  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document provides release notes for the input library. The changes include updates to dependencies, bug fixes, new features (like system prediction API support and increased prediction confidence), and API changes.

It also includes several API changes, including increasing the minimum supported SDK to 24, removing a no-op API, and renaming OutcomeReceiverCompat.

It specifies that the feature is accessible only in the latest stable channel version of Android Studio and the major versions (including patches) released within the preceding 10 months. This is crucial for developers to ensure they are using a compatible Android Studio version to access and utilize Play Policy Insights effectively.

entries.title: Older releases
entries.summary: This document details changes to Android Studio releases, specifically focusing on versions 3.6 and lower. The updates include improvements to design tools, such as split view in editors and enhancements to the Resource Manager. It also highlights updates to the Android Gradle plugin, including view binding, and native tooling improvements for Kotlin and JNI development. The document also describes the improvements in debugging and profiling tools.

entries.title: Older releases
entries.summary: The design tools now include a split view for simultaneous design and code editing. The Zoom and Pan controls are grouped in the bottom right corner of the editor window. The color picker provides color resource values and the resource manager has better searching capabilities, supports more resource types, and allows renaming resources during import.

entries.title: Older releases
entries.summary: The Android Gradle plugin now supports View Binding, allowing easier interaction with views. The plugin also provides enhancements for Apply Changes and a Refactor menu option to enable Instant Apps support and also includes optimizations for build speed, support for the Maven publishing plugin, and support for View Binding.

entries.title: Older releases
entries.summary: The APK Analyzer now allows deobfuscation of class and method bytecode. It also allows Kotlin-only APK source attachment for profiling and debugging pre-built APKs and has improved leak detection for Activity and Fragment instances.

entries.title: Older releases
entries.summary: Improvements for native (C/C++) development in Android Studio, including enhanced Kotlin support for JNI development (navigation, stub creation, warnings for unused functions, and refactoring), and also enhanced JNI improvements. It has APK reloading for native libraries. It is also possible to attach Kotlin-only external APK sources when you profile and debug pre-built APKs.

entries.title: Behavior changes: Apps targeting Android 14 or higher  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document details behavior changes for Android 14, focusing on core functionality and privacy. Key changes include required foreground service types, enforcement of the BLUETOOTH_CONNECT permission, updates to OpenJDK 17 affecting regular expressions and UUID handling, stricter JobScheduler behavior, and adjustments to media access permissions.

entries.title: Behavior changes: all apps
entries.summary: This document describes the behavior changes in Android 14 that affect all apps, regardless of their target SDK. Key changes include modifications to exact alarm permissions, context-registered broadcast queuing, app process killing behavior, Bluetooth MTU handling, app standby bucket assignment, mlock memory limits, cached app resource usage, and the dismissibility of ongoing foreground notifications.

entries.title: Data safety information is more visible
entries.summary: Android 14 enhances data safety visibility by displaying information declared in the Play Console form in more system locations, particularly regarding location data sharing. It introduces a system notification when an app broadens its location-sharing practices and provides a dedicated page in Settings to review and manage these changes. The changes aim to increase user awareness and control over their data sharing.

entries.title: Schedule exact alarms are denied by default  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Features and APIs Overview  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document introduces the features and APIs available in Android 14. The update includes enhancements to internationalization (per-app language preferences, Grammatical Inflection API, and regional preferences), accessibility (nonlinear font scaling and sp units), Ultra HDR for images, and camera extensions. These updates provide developers with tools to create more user-centric, accessible, and visually appealing applications.

entries.title: Schema for app metadata bundles  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Large screen device manufacturer per-app overrides  |  Android Developers

It details new `PackageManager.Property` tags introduced in Android 14 that allow apps to disable specific overrides, such as those related to resizing and aspect ratios. The updates include new code samples and additional descriptions of the impact of the described overrides.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes
entries.summary: Android 7.0 introduces enhanced Doze mode, extending battery life by restricting CPU and network activity even when the device is not stationary. It also removes implicit broadcasts (CONNECTIVITY_ACTION, ACTION_NEW_PICTURE, and ACTION_NEW_VIDEO) to optimize memory and power consumption. Apps targeting Android 7.0 and higher should adapt to these changes by using alternative mechanisms like JobScheduler and FileProvider, as implicit broadcasts are no longer guaranteed.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes
entries.summary: Android 7.0 enforces stricter file access permissions, restricting access to private app directories, triggering SecurityException when attempting to relax private file permissions or share file:// URIs. The DownloadManager also has changes. Developers should use content:// URIs and the FileProvider to share files between apps. Apps targeting Android 7.0 should adapt their file-sharing practices to avoid FileUriExposedException.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes
entries.summary: Android 7.0 enforces the StrictMode API policy, prohibiting the exposure of file:// URIs outside an app. To share files, developers should use content:// URIs and grant temporary access permissions, preferably using the FileProvider class. This change prevents FileUriExposedException and promotes secure file sharing.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes
entries.summary: Android 7.0 includes accessibility improvements, particularly a screen zoom feature that allows users to magnify the display. This feature dynamically changes the size of all screen elements, improving accessibility for users with low vision. Developers should test their apps to ensure they render correctly at various display sizes.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.1.0 (April 2016)
entries.summary: This release adds support for the N Developer Preview, JDK 8 and Java 8 language features using the Jack toolchain, incremental Java compilation, and dexing-in-process to improve build speeds. It also includes new links for Instant Run and Java 8 language features.

entries.title: Android Gradle Plugin 2.2.0 (September 2016)
entries.summary: This release of the Android Gradle Plugin includes updates to Gradle, introduces features for native code compilation with CMake and ndk-build, adds auto-download for missing SDK components, provides an experimental build cache, improves APK signing with v2 scheme, enhances multidex support with ProGuard rules for the main DEX file, and introduces the extractNativeLibs flag.  It also includes improvements to the Jack compiler with support for Jacoco test coverage and improved annotation processor support, and adjusts the default behavior of the Jack compiler to run in the same process as Gradle when the daemon heap size is sufficient, and provides a way to adjust the heap size.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: Android Gradle Plugin 3.0.0 introduces significant performance improvements, new features, and changes to the build process. Key improvements include faster build times through better parallelism, dependency management, per-class dexing, and cached output usage. New features include variant-aware dependency management, support for Android Instant Apps, built-in Java 8 support (with Jack deprecation), and enhanced testing capabilities with Android Test Orchestrator. These changes require Gradle 4.1 and SDK Build Tools 26.0.2 or higher, and developers should carefully consider project migration before adopting this version.

entries.title: Android Studio  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: Android 7.0 enhances Doze mode and optimizes background processes to conserve battery and reduce RAM usage. Apps targeting Android 7.0 and higher are restricted from receiving certain implicit broadcasts, such as `CONNECTIVITY_ACTION`, unless registered with `registerReceiver()`. Also, the system no longer sends `ACTION_NEW_PICTURE` or `ACTION_NEW_VIDEO` broadcasts. These changes require developers to use alternative mechanisms like `JobScheduler` for network operations.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: To enhance security, Android 7.0 restricts access to private app directories, triggering `SecurityException` if apps attempt to modify permissions using `MODE_WORLD_READABLE` or `MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE`. Furthermore, `file://` URIs are prohibited from being exposed outside the app's domain, and the `DownloadManager` can no longer share private files by filename, throwing `FileUriExposedException` and `SecurityException` respectively. Developers must use `FileProvider` and `ContentResolver.openFileDescriptor()` for secure file sharing.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: Apps targeting Android 7.0 must use `content://` URIs and grant temporary access permissions when sharing files between apps, enforced by the `StrictMode` API. Use of `FileProvider` is recommended to facilitate secure file sharing, as `file://` URIs are no longer allowed.

entries.title: Android 7.0 Behavior Changes  |  Android Developers

entries.title: Common problems and solutions
entries.summary: The document explains that using `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64` with older API levels may result in fewer functions being available. This is because `mmap64` was not available until Android 21. If the `minSdkVersion` is lower than 21, the C library does not contain an `mmap` that is compatible with `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64`.

entries.title: Common problems and solutions
entries.summary: The document provides a solution to the problem where exceptions are not being caught or `dynamic_cast` is failing across shared library boundaries. The recommended solution is to add a key function to your types. When a type does not have a key function, its typeinfo is emitted as a weak symbol and matching type infos are merged when libraries are loaded. When loading libraries dynamically, it may not be possible for the loader to merge type infos for the loaded libraries.
