entries.title: TV design review
entries.summary: The documentation for the TV design review prompt has been updated. The changes involve minor formatting adjustments, including the addition of a 'NOTE' callout and a slight modification to the instructions for running the prompt in Android Studio. These updates improve the clarity and presentation of the instructions.

entries.title: Validate handling of configuration changes
entries.summary: The documentation for the Android Studio prompt regarding handling configuration changes has been updated. The change replaces the original prompt with a note and updates the instructions on how to use the prompt in Android Studio.

entries.title: Sign your app
entries.summary: This document provides an overview of app signing in Android, emphasizing the importance of digital signatures for app installation and updates. It details the process of signing apps for release, including the use of Android App Bundles and Play App Signing, and explains the roles of app signing keys and upload keys. The document also highlights the benefits of using Play App Signing, such as improved security and the ability to use advanced delivery modes.

entries.title: Play Policy Insights in Android Studio
entries.summary: The documentation for Play Policy Insights has been updated with improved clarity and formatting. Key changes include adding a note about Android Studio version compatibility, rephrasing for better readability, and clarifying the purpose of the lint checks, emphasizing the importance of policy review and providing additional warnings when disabling lint checks.

entries.title: Upload your app to the Play Console
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to clarify requirements before uploading an app, including Play App Signing and Google Play's size limits. It also adds better formatting, adds a link to the Play Console upload process, and provides additional explanations of internal app distribution options.

entries.title: Emulator release notes
entries.summary: The documentation updates include changes to the formatting of notes and cautions using the `> [!NOTE]` and `> [!CAUTION]` markdown syntax. These changes improve the visual presentation of important information, making it easier for users to understand key details and warnings related to emulator usage.

entries.title: Android Studio Arctic Fox
entries.summary: This document describes the changes in Android Studio Arctic Fox. Key changes include a new versioning scheme, updates to the Android Gradle plugin, a new Background Task Inspector for WorkManager, and Database Inspector improvements.

entries.title: Android Studio Bumblebee
entries.summary: This document describes changes and improvements to the Android Studio Bumblebee release. Key changes include updates to the Device Manager instructions, a note regarding the Layout Inspector, and the migration of functionality from the Energy profiler to the Background task inspector. These updates provide better clarity, improve performance, and enhance debugging capabilities.

entries.title: Android Studio Chipmunk
entries.summary: This document describes the changes made in Android Studio Chipmunk. The changes include updates to Jetpack Compose support, enhanced profiling capabilities, and platform support for Android 13 APIs, along with bug fixes.

entries.title: Android Studio Dolphin
entries.summary: Android Studio Dolphin introduces several enhancements, including improved Compose tooling with animation coordination and recomposition count visualization in the Layout Inspector. It also updates Wear OS emulator pairing, adds new toolbar buttons for common actions, and provides new run configurations. Logcat receives major updates with enhanced formatting, multi-window support, view presets, and a new key-value search system for more efficient log analysis.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: This document describes the new features and improvements in Android Studio Electric Eel. Key updates include enhancements to Logcat, integration with Firebase Crashlytics for app quality insights, live updates for Compose Preview, support for different devices in Compose Preview, recomposition rendering highlights in the Layout Inspector, and visual linting for views.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: The new version of Logcat is enabled by default, improving log parsing, querying, and tracking.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: Android Studio now integrates with Firebase Crashlytics, allowing developers to view and address crash data directly within the IDE. This includes highlighted code lines, stack trace navigation, and filtering options.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: This integration streamlines the debugging process by bringing crash data directly into the development environment, improving app performance, and minimizing disruptions for users.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: Compose Previews now update immediately as changes are made.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: The `device` parameter in the Preview annotation can now be used to configure Composables for different devices.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: Recompositions are highlighted in the Layout Inspector to help identify areas of the UI that are recomposing.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: Android Studio now checks for visual lint issues across different screen sizes.

entries.title: Android Studio Electric Eel
entries.summary: The document mentions that the universal problems panel is available but doesn't provide enough information to create a meaningful summary.

entries.title: Android Studio Flamingo
entries.summary: This document describes the new features and improvements in Android Studio Flamingo. Key updates include enhancements to themed app icons and dynamic color previews in both Compose and XML, updates to Live Edit with manual and automatic modes, the introduction of Compose Tracing for performance analysis, new project templates, and device mirroring for streamlined development. These features aim to improve developer productivity and provide better tools for creating modern Android applications.

entries.title: Android Studio Giraffe
entries.summary: This document describes the new features and improvements introduced in Android Studio Giraffe, including Live Edit for Compose, a new UI theme, enhanced Compose Animation Preview support, the Grammatical Inflection API, an updated Device Explorer, a new Android SDK Upgrade Assistant, enhanced diagnostic tools, a Make Selected Modules toolbar button, and download information during sync.

entries.title: Android Studio Hedgehog
entries.summary: Android Studio Hedgehog introduces several new features, including integration of Android vitals data within App Quality Insights, a new Power Profiler to monitor device power consumption, an updated App Links Assistant for managing deep links, a new shortcut for Live Edit manual mode, new Compose Multipreview templates and Gallery mode, improved Compose state information in the debugger, and the ability to mirror physical devices within Android Studio.

entries.title: Android Studio Koala Feature Drop
entries.summary: This update introduces code block formatting changes within the 'as-koala-feature-drop-release-notes.md' document. Specifically, it updates the code syntax to include correct code block identifiers, which improves readability and code parsing.

entries.title: Android Studio Koala
entries.summary: Android Studio Koala release notes were updated to reflect the new features and improvements. Specifically, the Gemini API template, side-by-side layout in the Running Devices window, and IntelliJ 2024.1 platform updates are highlighted. These enhancements provide developers with tools for building AI-powered apps, improved device management, and a more feature-rich development environment.

entries.title: Android Studio Ladybug Feature Drop
entries.summary: This release note details new features in Android Studio Ladybug Feature Drop, including Wear Tiles Animation Preview, Motion Editor deprecation, new Gemini-powered features, Google Play SDK Index integration enhancements, mock sensor capabilities, App Links Assistant improvements, and notifications for missing build steps in run configurations. These updates aim to enhance developer productivity, improve debugging, and streamline app development workflows.

entries.title: Android Studio Ladybug
entries.summary: This release of Android Studio Ladybug includes updates to the IntelliJ platform and support for Pixel 9 series devices. The IntelliJ update brings improvements like enhanced Kotlin stability and IDE startup efficiency.  Android Studio now includes device definitions for the Pixel 9 series, allowing developers to test their applications on virtual devices representing the new hardware, ensuring compatibility across different screen sizes and device types.

entries.title: Android Studio Meerkat Feature Drop
entries.summary: This document describes new features in Android Studio Meerkat Feature Drop. These include improvements to themed icon previews, changes to Android Studio configuration directories, a new Prompt Library feature for Gemini, and the deprecation of the Motion Editor in favor of Jetpack Compose for animations.

entries.title: Android Studio Meerkat
entries.summary: Android Studio Meerkat introduces several enhancements and new features. Key improvements include Compose Preview enhancements (smoother zoom, collapsible groups, and view modes), streamlined KMP Shared Module integration, an improved UX for device management, new Gemini features, and updates to the Build menu and actions. Additionally, the release incorporates Google Play SDK Insights for deprecated SDK warnings, helping developers stay informed about SDK deprecations and alternatives.

entries.title: Android Studio Narwhal 3 Feature Drop
entries.summary: This document outlines new features in Android Studio Narwhal 3 Feature Drop. Key changes include dynamic resizing for Compose previews, a setting to display build files under corresponding modules in the Android view, the inclusion of Play Policy Insights as lint checks, and the ability to generate and restore app backups for testing purposes.

entries.title: Android Studio Narwhal 4 Feature Drop
entries.summary: This update to Android Studio Narwhal 4 Feature Drop includes new features and improvements. Key changes include a new setting to open projects in Project view by default, Gemini in Android Studio updates (stable Agent Mode, Ask mode renaming, and image support), Android SDK Upgrade Assistant support for Android 16, and enhanced Watch Face Format support with direct XML editing, code completion, and deployment capabilities.

entries.title: Android Studio Narwhal Feature Drop
entries.summary: This document describes the new features and improvements in the Android Studio Narwhal Feature Drop, including enhancements to Gemini in Agent Mode, new features for XR development (embedded XR Emulator, XR project template, and embedded Layout Inspector), support for 16 KB page sizes, Compose preview improvements, and the use of K2 Kotlin compiler by default. Additionally, it mentions the availability of Partner Device Labs and the Compose preview picker.

entries.title: Android Studio Narwhal
entries.summary: Android Studio Narwhal introduces new features including Gemini for businesses, Studio Labs for experimenting with AI features, and enhancements to the Embedded Layout Inspector component tree. The Layout Inspector improvements include horizontal scrolling, automatic scrolling on selection, and refined relationship visualization within the component tree, aimed at providing a more efficient debugging experience.

entries.title: Android Studio Otter 2 Feature Drop (December 2025)
entries.summary: This document describes new features in Android Studio Otter 2 Feature Drop. Key changes include updating the title and URL to use a direct link, refining the Android Knowledge Base's description, and updating the communications opt-in image URL.

entries.title: Android Studio Otter
entries.summary: This document describes the new backup and sync feature in Android Studio Otter. Users can now back up their Android Studio settings, such as keymaps and editor settings, to cloud storage using either their Google or JetBrains account. This feature allows users to sync their settings across different installations of Android Studio or IntelliJ products.

entries.title: Android Studio release names
entries.summary: The document has been updated to clarify the distinction between Merge and Feature Drop releases. Merge releases, which initiate a new animal cycle, incorporate the latest IntelliJ updates and may include limited Android-Studio-specific features, while Feature Drop releases, following the first release in the cycle, introduce new Android Studio features and bug fixes. The update provides clearer definitions and examples of these release types, enhancing understanding of the Android Studio release strategy.

entries.title: Report a bug
entries.summary: The documentation for reporting bugs in Android Studio has been updated with clearer instructions, including guidance on how to avoid reporting already fixed bugs and how to include necessary diagnostic information such as CPU profiles and memory usage reports. Formatting and wording were updated for clarity. The documentation also includes steps to generate thread dumps for debugging.

entries.title: Build and run your app

entries.title: Advanced emulator usage

The text has been slightly reworded for better readability and to ensure the links work.

entries.title: Android Device Streaming, powered by Firebase

Several notes and warnings have been updated to use the correct formatting and the usage of specific command-line options are clarified.

The changes include more explicit language about the use case of installing APKs and adding files. The text was also slightly reworded for clarity and conciseness, and some formatting changes were made. This is important to ensure users have clear instructions for sideloading apps and transferring files to the emulator for testing and development purposes.

entries.title: Launch the emulator in a separate window
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to clarify that the Android Emulator runs inside Android Studio by default and why this is beneficial. It explains how to launch the emulator in a separate window to access certain features. This change provides a clearer understanding of the default behavior and how to change it for specific use cases.

entries.title: Launch the emulator without launching an app
entries.summary: The documentation clarifies the scenario where launching the emulator without an app is useful, such as testing Bluetooth interactions. It also includes minor wording adjustments for better readability.

entries.title: Record the screen

entries.title: Snapshots

Specifically, the steps for saving Quick Boot snapshots were clarified and a note was added about skipping automatic saves. Also, the text was formatted for readability, and minor clarifications were made throughout the document.

entries.title: Take screenshots
entries.summary: The documentation for taking screenshots in the Android Emulator was updated. The changes include clarification on how to use the 'Take Screenshot' dialog, detailing the options available for editing, saving, and the naming convention of the generated PNG files. Additionally, the formatting of the command-line options was updated.

entries.title: Troubleshoot known issues with Android Emulator
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to improve clarity, fix formatting issues, and provide more accurate troubleshooting advice. Notably, it changes the initial introductory paragraph, updates troubleshooting steps for slow emulator performance, and adds better formatting.

entries.title: Camera support
entries.summary: The documentation for Android Emulator camera functionality was updated. The changes include improvements in formatting and wording, and minor modifications to the instructions for using the virtual scene camera and macros.

entries.title: Run apps on the Android Emulator
entries.summary: This document provides an overview of the Android Emulator, explaining its advantages, setup, and usage for testing Android applications. It also covers system requirements, AVD creation, and app deployment on the emulator.

entries.title: Test on multiple screen sizes with the resizable emulator
entries.summary: The documentation for the resizable emulator has been updated. The note about the emulator no longer being experimental is now emphasized, and there are some minor wording adjustments for clarity. This is important as it indicates the feature is now stable and ready for wider use.

entries.title: Service integrations in Android Studio
entries.summary: The documentation for Android Studio service integrations has been updated to improve readability and formatting. The changes include improvements in text layout, link formatting, and table formatting.

entries.summary: The documentation details deprecated Android Studio service integrations. Specifically, it lists integrations such as Meerkat, Cloud Source Repositories project import, and App Engine support, which are scheduled for removal starting in the Narwhal Feature Drop. Additionally, it mentions the deprecation of "Run with Firebase Test Lab", slated for removal in Android Studio "O" Feature Drop. These services are no longer supported in newer versions of Android Studio.

entries.title: Test your app

These tools offer various approaches to testing Android applications, from interactive recording to automated user action testing and stress testing. These tools help developers to automate the process of testing their apps.

entries.title: App Crawler
entries.summary: This document describes the App Crawler tool, which is used for automatically testing Android apps. The changes mostly refine the existing content by improving formatting, clarifying language, and updating links.

entries.title: Test in Android Studio
entries.summary: This document was updated to use a more modern syntax for emphasis, fix broken links, and improve clarity. It also adds a note to clarify the inclusion of Android framework APIs in local unit tests.

entries.title: Troubleshoot Android Studio
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to clarify and correct information related to high-density displays on Windows and Linux, including scaling factor settings, blurry/pixelated element issues, and incorrect element sizing. Also, the document was updated to use more correct paths for Windows directories.

entries.title: Write your app
entries.summary: The documentation was updated with minor text adjustments. It changed the wording in several sections and included minor formatting adjustments. There are no functional changes.

entries.title: Add app resources
entries.summary: This document provides a comprehensive guide on managing Android app resources, including adding, organizing, and merging them. It has been updated with detailed instructions on adding XML resources, resource directories, changing resource locations, and understanding the resource merging process, along with links to relevant documentation.

entries.title: Create WebP images
entries.summary: This document provides an overview of WebP image format, its benefits, and how to convert images to and from WebP format using Android Studio. The changes include improved formatting, more informative descriptions, and clearer steps for image conversion, enhancing the user experience.

entries.title: Connect to Firebase
entries.summary: This document provides instructions on how to connect an Android app to Firebase using the Assistant tool window in Android Studio. The changes include minor formatting adjustments, such as line breaks for better readability, and some rewording for clarity. These changes aim to improve the presentation and clarity of the instructions for developers integrating Firebase services into their apps.

entries.title: Develop a UI with Views
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to reflect the recommendation of building UI with Compose instead of Views. Minor formatting changes and clarifications have also been added for better readability. The document also includes updates to the buttons in the layout editor toolbar.

entries.title: Build animation with the Motion Editor
entries.summary: The Motion Editor documentation has been updated to reflect its deprecation in Android Studio Meerkat. A deprecation warning has been added at the beginning of the document.

entries.title: Manage your app's UI resources with Resource Manager
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to improve readability and clarity. Changes include formatting adjustments, more descriptive text, and minor updates to the import process description.  The addition of the 'drawable' drag and drop feature descriptions are particularly important to help users to understand the resource manager functionality better.

entries.title: Tools attributes reference
entries.summary: This document describes the `tools` namespace attributes in Android Studio for design-time and compile-time features. It details attributes for lint suppression, API level targeting, locale specification, design-time view customization, and layout preview behavior within the Android Studio layout editor. The document has been updated with minor text improvements and formatting changes.

entries.title: Generic System Image releases
entries.summary: This document introduces Android 17 GSI releases, including links to download images and associated terms and conditions. It provides details on the binaries, supported devices, and license agreements for usage. It is a new section to the documentation.

entries.title: Releases
entries.summary: This document was updated to include information about Android 15. Specifically, apps using the Android for Cars App Library must update to version 1.7.0-rc01 or later to prevent crashes on Android 15 due to secured background activity launch changes when permission dialogs are triggered. The document also reiterates the importance of testing apps for proper rendering due to window inset changes in Android 15, and provides a link to relevant documentation.

entries.title: Features and APIs
entries.summary: This document introduces the UWB Downlink-TDoA API for Android 17. It details how to initialize the Ranging Manager, verify device capabilities, start a DL-TDoA session, and configure parameters using both Kotlin and Java code examples. It also provides guidance on Out-of-Band (OOB) configurations for Wi-Fi and BLE, as well as alternative parameter building methods.

entries.title: Android Bench
entries.summary: This new documentation introduces "Android Bench," a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the capabilities of LLMs in Android development, addressing challenges not covered by existing benchmarks.

entries.title: Android Bench
entries.summary: This new documentation, "methodology.md," details the Android Bench benchmark, outlining its goals, methodology, and composition for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) in Android development. It aims to encourage LLM improvements and empower developers with AI assistance.

entries.title: Components
entries.summary: The documentation for AI glasses components has been updated to provide a more detailed explanation of the optimizations made for transparent displays. The changes include specifying that surfaces use transparency by changing the surface color to black to make it transparent, adding details on outlines, highlights, shapes, typography, and iconography. This helps developers understand the specific design considerations for building user interfaces on AI glasses, leading to better visual experiences.

entries.title: Get started
entries.summary: This document provides a guide to building AI Glasses apps using the Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI framework.  The changes primarily involve minor wording adjustments for clarity, formatting, and improved image alt text. The core content and guidance on design principles, user journeys, audio flows, and system UI remain consistent.

entries.title: Range between devices
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to include information about the UWB Downlink-TDoA API. This addition provides a link to the Android 17 features page, offering developers details about the new API for utilizing UWB technology to measure distance and location with improved accuracy.

entries.title: Develop spatial UI with Jetpack Compose for XR
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to reflect the addition of `PlanarEmbeddedSubspace` and changes to the `Subspace` composable.  `PlanarEmbeddedSubspace` allows for the integration of 3D content within a 2D layout, offering greater flexibility. Also, the documentation clarifies `Subspace` behavior and the importance of using subspace composables within the appropriate context. These changes provide developers with additional options for spatial UI design and clarify existing usage patterns.

entries.title: Play Games PC samples
entries.summary: This new documentation page introduces code samples designed to help developers quickly integrate Play Games PC features into their games. It includes samples for Play Billing integration and demonstrates the use of the Play PC SDK within a Unity project.

entries.title: Subscription lifecycle
entries.summary: The documentation for subscriptions.md was updated to replace all instances of "**Note:**" and "**Warning:**" with blockquotes using "[!NOTE]" and "[!WARNING]" respectively. This change improves the visual presentation and readability of the document by using a more structured format for important notes and warnings. Additionally, there was a minor change in the cancellation type from `USER_REQUESTED_STOP_RENEWALS` to `USER_REQUESTED_STOP_RENEWALS`.

entries.title: Manage subscriptions and one-time purchases
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to reflect the change of `cancellationType` value from `USER_REQUESTED_STOP_RENEWAL` to `USER_REQUESTED_STOP_RENEWALS` when cancelling a subscription. Additionally, the documentation now uses the NOTE formatting style. Also, clarification has been added regarding subscription revoking via API calls, especially for the installment subscriptions.

entries.title: Implement Sign in with Google
entries.summary: This new documentation page provides a guide on how to implement Sign in with Google using the Credential Manager on Android, covering steps from adding dependencies to handling sign-out.

entries.title: About Sign in with Google
entries.summary: This document provides an overview of integrating Sign in with Google using Credential Manager. It highlights the benefits, user interface guidelines, and prerequisites for implementing the feature, including version compatibility and links to relevant documentation.

entries.title: About the migration from legacy Google Sign-In
entries.summary: This document outlines the migration from legacy Google Sign-In for Android to the Android Credential Manager and AuthorizationClient API. The guide highlights the benefits of using Credential Manager, including a unified API, support for the Sign in with Google button, and streamlined sign-in flows. It also explains the differences between the legacy approach and the updated Credential Manager implementation, particularly in how authentication and authorization are handled.

entries.title: Android Mobile App Developer Tools - Android Developers
entries.summary: The documentation introduces 'Android Bench', an official benchmark for Large Language Models (LLMs) used in Android development, replacing the previous Google I/O announcement. This change provides developers with a dedicated resource for evaluating and comparing LLMs, which is critical for developers looking to integrate AI into their Android applications.

entries.title: navigation3
entries.summary: Version 1.1.0-alpha04 of androidx.navigation3 has been released. This release includes a new suspending callback `onRemoved` in the `OverlayScene` interface, which is invoked before the overlay scene is removed from composition.  Additionally, the `SceneStrategy` interface has been refactored with a new `SceneDecoratorStrategy` interface to manage scene decoration, along with new APIs for `NavDisplay` and `rememberSceneState`.

entries.title: Android Studio Nightly
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to reflect the latest nightly build. Specifically, the download links and version numbers were updated from 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-06.

entries.title: Updates to non-SDK interface restrictions in Android 10
entries.summary: This document outlines changes to non-SDK interface restrictions in Android 10. Key updates include renaming the lists of restricted interfaces based on the maximum target SDK version, adding code annotations for non-SDK interfaces, and modifications to the ADB commands for managing access to these interfaces. These changes aim to improve app stability and compatibility by encouraging the use of public SDK alternatives.

entries.title: Set up the 12L SDK
entries.summary: The documentation for setting up the 12L SDK has been updated with minor formatting changes and rewording for clarity. These changes include adjustments to spacing, line breaks, and emphasis, ensuring better readability of the instructions for developers.

entries.title: Set up the Android 12 SDK
entries.summary: This document provides instructions on setting up the Android 12 SDK in Android Studio, including selecting the correct SDK Platform and Build-Tools versions. It also explains how to update the app's build configuration to target Android 12 and links to resources about behavior changes and new APIs.

entries.title: Android 12 features and changes list

The content is presented in a table format, categorizing changes by areas like Activity lifecycle, Camera, Connectivity, Core functionality, and others. Each entry includes the category, type of change, and a description with a link to more detailed documentation.

entries.title: Android 13 features and changes list
entries.summary: This document outlines changes for Android 13 affecting app developers, detailing new features, API updates, and behavior changes across various categories like camera, connectivity, developer tools, graphics, media, and more.  The updates cover a wide range, from deprecated APIs to performance improvements and new user experience features.

entries.title: Schema for app metadata bundles

The primary change involves replacing all instances of the "Note:" style with the "NOTE:" callouts, and "Important:" to "IMPORTANT:" callouts, to improve readability. These changes do not affect the functionality of the schema itself but enhance the clarity of the documentation.

entries.title: Set up the Android 14 SDK
entries.summary: This document provides instructions on setting up the Android 14 SDK in Android Studio, including selecting the correct packages and updating the app's build configuration. It also provides links to further documentation regarding behavior changes and new features in Android 14. The changes involve formatting and minor wording updates for clarity.

It explains how to use the `androidx.lifecycle` package to create components that automatically adjust their behavior based on the lifecycle state of activities and fragments, promoting better code organization and maintainability.

entries.title: LiveData overview
entries.summary: The documentation for LiveData has been updated. The changes include improvements in formatting, the addition of the NOTE blocks, and minor rewording for clarity. The content remains largely the same, focusing on the core concepts and advantages of using LiveData.

entries.title: Paging 2 library overview
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to use the `[!CAUTION]` and `[!NOTE]` callout blocks for important information, improving readability and highlighting key points about the deprecated Paging library version. This change makes it easier for developers to quickly identify warnings and notes within the documentation.

entries.title: Gather paged data
entries.summary: The documentation was updated to reflect the deprecation of the Paging library and directs users to the Paging 3 guides. It also incorporates formatting changes, including the use of callout boxes and minor adjustments to existing content for improved clarity and readability.

entries.title: Manage and present loading states
entries.summary: This document describes how to manage and present loading states using the Paging library.  It explains how the library exposes loading states through the `LoadState` class and how to use listeners or adapters to display loading indicators in the UI. The changes include formatting updates, and clarifying language, and improved code samples.

entries.title: Test your Paging implementation
entries.summary: This document provides an updated guide on testing Paging library implementations. Key changes include enhanced explanations of UI layer tests with `asSnapshot()`, testing transformations with `asPagingSourceFactory()`, and data layer tests for `PagingSource` and `RemoteMediator`, along with improved code examples and clarifications.

entries.title: Display paged lists
entries.summary: The documentation updates the UI section of the Paging Library guide. It includes formatting improvements, clarifies the use of deprecated versions, and updates links. Additionally, it improves the formatting of code snippets and adds more detailed explanations about placeholders.

entries.title: Migrate to Paging 3
entries.summary: This document details the migration from Paging 2 to Paging 3, highlighting the key changes in components like DataSource, PagedList, and PagedListAdapter, as well as the benefits of adopting Paging 3.  It explains how to migrate each component, and mentions backwards compatibility allowing for a phased migration.  It also points to where to find additional information like defining a data source or the RecyclerView adapter.

entries.title: Page from network and database
entries.summary: This document introduces how to use Paging 3 library with a local database to improve user experience when network connections are unreliable. It explains how to coordinate data loads using RemoteMediator, the Paging lifecycle, and provides implementation examples using Room.

entries.title: Paging library overview
entries.summary: The documentation has been updated to use the standard Markdown callout syntax, replacing the bolded 'Note:' with a more structured '[!NOTE]' callout block. This change enhances readability and consistency with other documentation.

entries.title: Load and display paged data
entries.summary: This document provides a comprehensive guide on using the Paging library v3 to load and display paged data in an Android application. It covers defining data sources using `PagingSource`, setting up data streams with `Pager`, and implementing a `RecyclerView` adapter with `PagingDataAdapter`.

entries.title: Transform data streams
entries.summary: This document describes how to transform data streams when using the Paging library. It explains how to apply basic transformations like converting data types, filtering data, and adding list separators, along with code examples in Kotlin and Java. It emphasizes keeping repository and UI constructs separate and avoiding duplicate work by using the `cachedIn()` operation.

entries.title: Architecture Component Release Notes

entries.title: ViewModel overview

The guide also clarifies ViewModel usage within Jetpack Compose and provides implementation examples.

entries.title: ViewModel Scoping APIs

entries.title: ViewModel APIs cheat sheet

entries.title: Data Binding Library

entries.title: Binding adapters

entries.title: Generated binding classes

The document also covers the use of converters and how to avoid infinite loops when implementing two-way data binding.

entries.title: View binding

entries.summary: Key changes include support for QR code provisioning, a work profile security challenge, the ability to disable app access, work mode toggling, always-on VPN configuration, improved contact integration, remote reboot capabilities, a location off switch, customized provisioning options, multiple Wi-Fi CA certificate support, customized lock screen messages, and work profile connection services.

entries.title: What's new in Android 7.0
entries.summary: These changes improve enterprise device management by providing administrators with more control over devices, enhancing security with features like work profile challenges and always-on VPN, and improving the user experience with features like contact integration and the work mode toggle. This enables more secure and manageable corporate environments.

entries.title: What's new in Android 8.0
entries.summary: Android 8.0 introduces significant enhancements for enterprise Android deployments. Key changes include the ability to create work profiles on fully managed devices, enabling better separation of work and personal data. Additionally, user affiliation features allow for more device-wide control and functionality based on organizational identity. Several security improvements are also included, such as enhanced password reset and network logging capabilities.

entries.title: What’s in Android 9 for enterprise apps
entries.summary: This document outlines the enterprise-focused changes in Android 9. Key updates include UI enhancements for work profiles, APIs for cross-profile app switching, and expanded lock task mode capabilities. These changes aim to improve user experience and control in managed device scenarios.

entries.title: behavior-changes-all.md
entries.summary: Android 17 introduces a limit on the number of keys an app can create in the Android Keystore. Non-system apps targeting Android 17 or higher are limited to 50,000 keys, while all other apps, including system apps, are limited to 200,000 keys. If an app exceeds this limit, key creation will fail with a KeyStoreException, and the getNumericErrorCode() method will return different error codes depending on the target API level. This change prevents apps from creating an excessive number of keys, which could impact the performance of other apps on the device.

entries.title: Contact picker
entries.summary: This document introduces the Android Contact Picker, a privacy-focused and standardized interface for apps to request contact information from users. The Contact Picker, available on Android 17 (Jelly Bean) and later, provides a secure alternative to requesting the broad `READ_CONTACTS` permission. Instead of accessing the entire address book, apps specify the required data fields (e.g., phone numbers, email addresses), and the user selects which contacts to share. The document explains how to integrate the Contact Picker using `Intent.ACTION_PICK_CONTACTS` and `Intent.EXTRA_REQUESTED_DATA_FIELDS` to specify the desired contact data (using MIME types from `ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds`). It provides Kotlin and Java code examples for launching the picker in both single and multi-selection modes (using `Intent.EXTRA_ALLOW_MULTIPLE` and `Intent.EXTRA_SELECTION_LIMIT`). The document also details how to handle results, including how to query the returned `Session URI` using a `ContentResolver` to access the selected contact data, demonstrating how to process the retrieved data using a `Cursor`. It includes important considerations such as backward compatibility with the legacy `ACTION_PICK` intent, testing on older SDKs (using `EXTRA_USE_SYSTEM_CONTACTS_PICKER`), and best practices: Requesting only necessary data fields; persisting data immediately (as the session URI grants temporary access); and avoiding reliance on account data due to privacy protections.  This documentation aims to guide developers in using the Contact Picker to enhance user privacy and offer a consistent and user-friendly contact sharing experience.

entries.title: FlexBox
entries.summary: This document introduces `FlexBox` in Android Compose, a layout container for arranging items in a single direction (horizontal or vertical). It's designed to resize, wrap, align, and distribute space among items to optimize the use of available space, making it suitable for layouts with varying item sizes and responsiveness to screen size changes. The document emphasizes that `FlexBox` is heavily influenced by the CSS Flexible Box Layout specification, sharing similar concepts like main and cross axes, main and cross sizes, and terminology such as 'grow', 'shrink', and 'basis'. The document explains when to use `FlexBox` (displaying a small number of items within a larger layout, or when wrapping items) and when not to (for large numbers of items, use lazy lists/grids or for overall screen layouts, use `Grid`). It details how to apply properties to the `FlexBox` container (e.g., direction, wrap, justifyContent, alignItems) and individual items (e.g., basis, grow, shrink, alignSelf). Finally, the document outlines the layout algorithm of `FlexBox`, detailing the steps involved in calculating child sizes, sorting items, building lines, and aligning/resizing items on both the main and cross axes. It includes links to other guides for container and item behaviors, and for getting started with `FlexBox`.

entries.title: Set container behavior
entries.summary: This document introduces the configuration options for the `FlexBox` container in Android Compose, a layout element used for arranging items in a flexible manner. It explains how to customize `FlexBox` behavior using a `FlexBoxConfig` block. The primary focus is on the properties within `FlexBoxConfig` that control the layout: `direction`, `alignItems`, `alignContent`, `justifyContent`, `wrap`, `rowGap`, `columnGap`, and `gap`.  The `direction` property sets the main axis (either `Row` or `Column`, with reverse variants), determining the primary direction items are laid out.  `justifyContent` is used to align and distribute items along the main axis, offering options like `Start`, `Center`, `End`, `SpaceBetween`, `SpaceAround`, and `SpaceEvenly`.  `alignItems` controls alignment along the cross axis within a single line, providing options like `Start`, `End`, `Center`, `Stretch`, and `Baseline`.  `alignContent` manages the alignment and spacing of multiple lines (when wrapping is enabled), offering similar options to `justifyContent`.  The `wrap` property enables multi-line layouts; options include `NoWrap`, `Wrap`, and `WrapReverse`.  Finally, the document covers adding gaps between items using `rowGap`, `columnGap`, or the combined `gap` function. The documentation uses visual aids to illustrate the effects of different configuration options, including images showcasing the impact of each property on the item arrangement within the `FlexBox` container. This is a comprehensive guide to utilizing `FlexBox` effectively within Compose layouts.

entries.title: Get started with FlexBox
entries.summary: This document, titled "get-started.md," provides a beginner's guide to implementing basic `FlexBox` layouts in Android Compose. It begins by outlining the necessary steps for setting up the project, which includes adding the `androidx.compose.foundation.layout` library to the project's `lib.versions.toml` and then adding the library dependency to the app's `build.gradle.kts` file. The document then presents two examples to illustrate how `FlexBox` can be used to create layouts. The first example demonstrates a simple `FlexBox` layout with two `Text` elements stacked vertically and center-aligned. The second example showcases a more complex layout, where `FlexBox` wraps five items onto two rows, allowing them to grow unequally to fill the available space with a specified gap between items. Images are included to visualize the resulting layouts. The document concludes by directing readers to further documentation for in-depth information on `FlexBox` behavior, specifically referencing resources on "Set container behavior" and "Set item behavior."

entries.title: Set item behavior
entries.summary:
This document introduces how to control the behavior of individual items within a `FlexBox` layout in Android Compose. It details the use of the `Modifier.flex` modifier to manipulate item size, alignment, and order. The core concepts revolve around three main aspects:

1.  **Item Size:** This section covers how to manage the size of items using `basis`, `grow`, and `shrink` properties.  `basis` defines the initial or preferred size.  Different value types such as `Auto`, fixed `dp`, and percentage are explained, including behavior and example code.  `grow` determines how much an item expands to fill extra space, with examples of how different grow values affect the layout.  `shrink` addresses how items contract when space is insufficient, also detailing its behavior and examples.
2.  **Item Alignment:** This explains how to use `alignSelf` to override the `alignItems` property of the parent `FlexBox` container for specific items. The document describes the possible values for `alignSelf` (including `Auto`) and provides example code, along with a visual representation of the effect of alignment.
3.  **Item Order:** This part describes how to change the visual order of items within the `FlexBox` layout using the `order` property.  It explains that items are laid out in the order they are declared by default and how `order` can be used to reorder them without changing the code's declaration order. Example code shows how items with different order values are displayed, illustrating the impact of `order` on the visual layout.

The document provides code snippets, diagrams, and descriptions to clarify the usage and effect of each property, providing a comprehensive guide to controlling item behavior within a `FlexBox` layout.

entries.title: Bubbles
entries.summary: This document introduces the Bubbles feature, a new windowing mode in Android that provides a floating UI experience, drawing parallels to the messaging bubbles API. Users can create app bubbles on phones, foldables, and tablets by long-pressing an app icon in the launcher. The document highlights the visual representation of this feature with an example of bubbling a calendar app, demonstrated through a GIF. On larger screens, a bubble bar is incorporated into the taskbar, allowing users to organize, switch between, and manage bubbles, including anchoring them to the screen. The document emphasizes that this Bubbles feature is accessible to all apps that adhere to existing best practices for multi-window support and encourages developers to follow the guidelines to ensure proper functionality of their apps as bubbles.

entries.title: Overview  |  Gallery  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document, titled "Gallery", is a new addition to the Android Developers documentation and serves as a curated showcase of app designs optimized for large screens like tablets and foldables. It emphasizes the importance of adapting app UIs for various screen sizes to enhance user experience. The document is structured to inspire developers with examples from different app categories. It highlights the benefits of optimizing apps for larger screens, such as showing more content, enabling multitasking, and providing more immersive experiences. The core content focuses on how to make apps look great on different screen sizes and provides examples from multiple app domains including social media, media, productivity, shopping, reading, creativity, and games. Each section provides a brief description of how to optimize the user experience within these categories. The document also links to resources for UI design and canonical layouts, encouraging developers to create immersive and user-friendly experiences for large-screen devices.

entries.title: Creativity  |  Gallery  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document, titled "Creativity," is a new addition to the Android Developers documentation, specifically within the "Large Screens" and "Gallery" sections. It serves as a guide for developers on how to leverage the larger screen real estate of tablets and other large-screen devices to enhance the creative experience for users. The document focuses on features that capitalize on the potential of a tablet as a creative canvas, particularly emphasizing stylus input. It highlights key stylus features such as low latency, hover capabilities, palm rejection, and tilt/pressure sensitivity, linking to relevant Android developer resources for further exploration. The document also provides guidance on optimizing the user interface for creativity-focused apps, including utilizing more workspace for tools like palettes and settings panels. It suggests context menus, customization of the workspace (movable and resizable elements), and differentiated experiences unique to large screens. Examples of these differentiated experiences include hover-to-display, multi-window functionality, hover-to-preview, and drag-and-drop support. The document concludes with a customer story from the Concepts app, demonstrating the positive impact of large-screen optimization on user engagement, and cross-references to other related content such as Games and Social media & comm.

entries.title: Games  |  Gallery  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document provides an overview of how to optimize Android games for large screens, such as tablets, foldables, and devices with external peripherals. It highlights key features and considerations for creating engaging gaming experiences on these platforms. The document emphasizes the growing popularity of large screens for mobile gaming and encourages developers to leverage the unique capabilities of these devices. The core topics covered include:  1.  **Continuity**: Ensuring uninterrupted gameplay across different orientations, postures, and window sizes by supporting configuration changes gracefully. The document links to resources on handling configuration changes and cross-device play.  2.  **Game Controller Integration**: Encouraging the integration of external game controllers to enhance the gaming experience, with links to relevant SDK documentation and support information.  3.  **Mouse, Trackpad, and Keyboard Support**: Providing guidelines for incorporating mouse, trackpad, and keyboard input for fine-tuned gameplay, particularly on ChromeOS and Google Play Games on PC, with links to input support documentation.  4.  **Differentiated Experiences**: Showcasing features unique to large screens, like multi-window mode for social gaming experiences, and foldables, with guidance on optimizing in-game views and utilizing multi-modal displays.  5.  **Supported Game Engines**: Listing and linking to information on popular game engines like Unity, Unreal Engine, and Cocos, that are optimizing for large screen and multiplatform experiences.  6.  **Why Build**: Providing rationale for developing for large screens, citing the increasing market share of foldable phones (projected to reach 41M shipments by 2026) and the investment by OEMs like Samsung, Microsoft, and Lenovo in large-screen devices.  The document concludes with links to other galleries on social media and media app optimization for large screens.

entries.title: Productivity  |  Gallery  |  Android Developers
entries.summary:
This document introduces a new page within the Android Developers documentation, specifically focusing on "Productivity" within the "Gallery" section for large screens. It serves as a guide for developers to design Android applications that enhance user productivity on devices with larger displays, such as tablets and foldables. The document's primary purpose is to showcase design patterns and best practices for creating productive and user-friendly experiences on large screens, highlighting features and capabilities not easily achievable on smaller screen devices.

The content is organized into several key sections:

1.  **Introduction:** Sets the context, emphasizing the importance of adapting apps for large screens to enhance productivity and provides links to related documentation.
2.  **Core Concepts and Layouts:** This section describes layout patterns tailored for productivity, including:
    *   **File browsing and filtering:** Displaying thumbnails for easy file navigation.
    *   **Items and overviews:** Showing detailed list information in conjunction with a list.
    *   **Tools and settings (Supporting Pane):** Providing easy access to more tools and settings without obstructing the main content.
    *   **Reviews and comments (Supporting Pane):** Incorporating reviews and comments directly within the document view.
    Each layout pattern includes links to relevant Material Design guidelines and implementation guides.
3.  **Differentiated Experiences:** This section covers features that leverage large-screen capabilities:
    *   **Drag and drop:** Enables intuitive content sharing between different views or apps.
    *   **Tabletop:** Designing layouts suitable for activities like presentations and video conferences.
    *   **Multi-window:** Facilitating multitasking with apps working side-by-side.
    *   **Keyboard, mouse, and trackpad:** Enhancing productivity through input device support.
4.  **Customer Stories:** Presents real-world examples of how large screen features have been implemented to improve user experience, including Chrome and WPS Office, with links to relevant articles.
5.  **Build better with Android:** Provides links to related galleries about shopping and reading.

The "why it matters" is that it helps developers provide enhanced user experiences on large-screen devices, enabling efficient multitasking, intuitive navigation, and overall improved productivity. This, in turn, can lead to increased user engagement and satisfaction, and positions applications for success in a market increasingly focused on devices like tablets and foldables. This document provides practical guidance and promotes best practices for designing and developing Android apps that take full advantage of large-screen capabilities.

entries.title: Reading  |  Gallery  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document, titled "Reading" within the "Gallery" section of Android Developers documentation, provides guidance and showcases design considerations for creating optimal reading experiences on large-screen Android devices, particularly tablets and foldables. It emphasizes the advantages large screens offer, such as improved readability and immersive experiences, and suggests ways to leverage these advantages. The document is structured to highlight key features and design patterns for reading applications. The core concepts include "Full-screen readability" via immersive mode to reduce distractions, "Booklists and buys" using multi-column grids and side navigation, and "What's inside" with synopses. It also covers "Complementary content" in supporting panes, "Markup tools," and "News feeds." Furthermore, the document explores "Differentiated experiences" unique to large screens. It highlights multi-window support for multitasking, the ability to mimic a physical book's layout with "Book posture" on foldables, and "Drag and drop" functionality for content manipulation. The document includes links to relevant Android developer documentation for implementation. The document also includes a customer story from Readera LLC emphasizing the positive impact of large-screen adaptation on user reading time. Finally, it links to other areas like "Creativity" and "Games" within the Large Screens Gallery, indicating broader design considerations beyond just reading.

entries.title: Shopping  |  Gallery  |  Android Developers
entries.summary: This document introduces a new page within the Android Developers documentation, specifically focusing on the "Shopping" use case within the "Gallery" section for large screens. It aims to guide developers on designing shopping applications that effectively utilize the increased screen real estate available on larger devices, such as tablets and foldables. The document's primary purpose is to showcase how to enhance the shopping experience on large screens. It details how adaptive apps can present product information, specifications, and related details efficiently. The document outlines core concepts such as "Product specs" (using list-detail layouts), "Catalogs and promotions" (using feed layouts), and "Supporting the sale" (using supporting pane layouts). Each section provides design considerations and links to relevant Material Design guidelines and implementation resources. Furthermore, the document highlights differentiated experiences like "Multi-window" and "Drag and drop," which are not readily available on smaller screens. Finally, the document includes a customer story about eBay, emphasizing how large-screen optimizations led to a higher Google Play rating.  The document concludes with recommendations and links to content about 'Reading' and 'Creativity' user cases.
